title: Drain consensus before Reth teardown
description: Fix the confirmed normal-SIGTERM lifecycle race exposed by Radicle release E2E r23. The outer Reth runner cancels the outbe launcher future before its inner cleanup runs, dropping OCOMP projection readiness while a follower Exact block acknowledgement is in flight. The unprocessed block remains unacknowledged and restart-safe, but Commonware marshal panics on Canceled. This is a separate lifecycle blocker; it is not a Radicle, fixture, projection-semantics, executor, or Commonware defect.
design: Frozen minimal seam: bin/outbe-chain/src/main.rs is the only production owner and hot file. Add an RAII consensus lifecycle guard created after the Reth NodeHandle and owning the cancellation token plus consensus JoinHandle. Drop, explicit completion, and launcher-future cancellation all perform the same ordering: signal Commonware shutdown, call context stop with a 5 second bounded drain, join consensus synchronously, then permit Reth/ExEx/engine teardown. No false ACK, no weakening ReadinessChannelClosed, no executor/stack/Commonware edits, no log whitelist. If RED proves another production path is necessary, stop and re-freeze before editing it.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic inline main.rs RED proves dropping a pending launcher lifecycle synchronously cancels and joins consensus before dependent execution resources are torn down; explicit join preserves consensus errors and panics. Existing finalized-block failure semantics remain unchanged. Release SGX/no-attest Radicle E2E passes all 17 functional steps with log_audit.clean=true; forced stop remains restart-safe and block 25 or its equivalent replays without a progress lie. Scope audit confirms only main.rs production semantics changed.

title: Run due Metadosis processing from the hourly WWD cycle
description: The dedicated Cycle WWD trigger currently advances phase status only. A WWD that reaches scheduled_process_time outside UTC midnight becomes Ready but is not processed until the next daily emission trigger. Change the production WWD cadence to hourly and make the dedicated trigger process due Ready work after advancing all active WWDs.
design:
Architecture freeze v1.

Scope: make the dedicated Cycle WWD trigger fire on UTC hour boundaries and execute a bounded WWD tick: validate the active Metadosis profile, inspect every active WWD against the canonical block timestamp, apply every due phase edge, then process the deterministically selected due Ready WWD through the existing local-terminal or OCOMP pre-admission path. Keep stable TriggerId value 2 and persisted Cycle cursor compatibility. Change the production default advance interval from 12 hours to 1 hour. Keep genesis test overrides authoritative when the feature is enabled.

Non-goals: no WWD phase-duration changes; no forming/lookback/offering/waiting boundary changes; no new storage or wire types; no trigger ID renumbering; no daily emission/allocation changes; no new WWD creation from the hourly handler; no OCOMP FSM change; no removal of the existing one-admission-per-tick bound; no genesis package regeneration or remote deployment in this code slice.

Invariants: (1) default WWD tick slots are epoch-aligned UTC hours, period 3600, offset 0; (2) every active WWD is examined on each fired tick and due nonterminal phase edges are applied exactly once by the existing reducer; (3) timestamps before a boundary are no-ops; (4) once scheduled_process_time is reached, the existing deterministic Ready selection is processed in the same authenticated Cycle handler; (5) an existing OCOMP FSM is validated and never duplicated; (6) completed, failed, and OffchainPending WWDs are not reprocessed; (7) at most one new READY/OCOMP admission is consumed per tick, preserving the current gas/capacity bound; any due backlog remains active for the next hourly tick; (8) hourly processing does not create a WorldwideDay or form/allocate its daily limit; those remain midnight-owned; (9) midnight ordering remains EmissionLimitDaily before the WWD tick, and replay in the same timestamp is idempotent; (10) handler failure rolls back its storage/CE checkpoint and leaves the Cycle cursor unchanged for retry.

Transition matrix: Forming before forming_end -> no-op; Forming at/after forming_end -> resolve forming and continue through every already-due edge; LookbackDelay before lookback_end -> no-op, otherwise open Offering; Offering before offering_end -> no-op, otherwise close to Waiting, and at/after scheduled_process_time become Ready; Waiting before scheduled_process_time -> no-op, at/after it become Ready; Ready without FSM -> local terminal completion/failure or OCOMP pre-admission according to existing settlement rules; Ready with FSM -> validate and skip duplicate admission; OffchainPending/Completed/Failed -> no-op; several due WWDs -> all safe phase edges are evaluated, existing one-admission ordering chooses at most one for processing and backlog retries next hourly tick; missed slots -> dispatcher advances one persisted slot per successful block until caught up; failure -> full trigger rollback and retry.

Canonical shapes and compatibility: TriggerId::WwdAdvanceNoon keeps numeric value 2; Cycle last_executed_at and last_executed_block_number mappings are unchanged; WWD/OCOMP types and bindings are unchanged. Internal handler naming/comments may be corrected without changing the emitted numeric ID. Existing persisted noon cursor becomes a valid last execution point under the hourly period and schedules the next UTC hour.

Ownership: outbe-chain-constants owns the default 3600-second interval; outbe-cycle triggers owns slot cadence and handler wiring; outbe-metadosis runtime/commands owns the advance-then-process tick without day creation; existing reducer owns phase correctness; existing settlement owns local/OCOMP Ready handling; Cycle dispatcher owns checkpoint/cursor retry.

Expected hot files: crates/blockchain/constants/src/lib.rs, crates/system/cycle/src/triggers.rs, crates/core/metadosis/src/runtime.rs, crates/core/metadosis/src/commands.rs; one implementation pass and at most one integration-correction pass each. Expected tests: constants default/override validation; trigger default hour alignment and custom interval; before-boundary no-op; exact scheduled boundary advances and processes in one hourly fire; all active WWD phase walk; no duplicate OCOMP admission; no hourly day creation; failure leaves cursor unchanged; midnight coexistence; focused metadosis/cycle tests plus fmt, clippy/check.

Ordered PR slice: tests for hourly cadence and due processing; minimal command/runtime seam; trigger/default wiring; focused validation; scope audit. Stop and re-plan if multiple-admission semantics, a new storage field/type, new trigger ID, daily allocation changes, or production paths outside this map become necessary.
acceptance_criteria: With production defaults, the dedicated WWD trigger fires at every UTC hour. Each fire advances all active WWDs whose phase boundary has passed and processes the selected WWD immediately when scheduled_process_time is due, without waiting for midnight, duplicating OCOMP work, creating a new WWD, or changing daily emission behavior. Focused tests and build checks pass.

title: Persist bounded OCOMP discovery scan checkpoint
description: SnapshotExporter polls finalized OffchainJobRequested logs every second. When no job has ever been found, its only cursor is absent, so every poll scans from block 1; after the chain exceeded the RPC 100000-block range limit discovery became permanently retrying. Add a separate durable scan watermark and bound each query to 100 blocks, then prepare the release outbe-ocomp binary.
design:
Architecture freeze v1.

Scope: fix FinalizedRpcDiscoveryV1 used by the external SnapshotExporter (and the same shared public-RPC discovery primitive) so successful empty scans advance durably in bounded 100-block finalized ranges. Add a separate scan checkpoint under the existing discovery journal root. Build a release outbe-ocomp binary. Non-goals: no genesis/ChainSpec change, no consensus or precompile behavior change, no Mongo schema change, no ZeroMQ redesign, no node/enclave build, no remote deployment.

Invariants:
1. RPC eth_getLogs range is never larger than 100 inclusive blocks.
2. Only finalized blocks may advance the scan checkpoint.
3. The checkpoint advances only after the complete queried range was successfully decoded and found to contain no unprocessed eligible job; discovery errors leave it unchanged.
4. Job authority (discovery.v1) remains separate from scan progress.
5. Restart trusts a checkpoint only after exact chain identity and canonical height/hash validation.
6. Missing checkpoint is backward-compatible: resume after the durable job cursor if present, otherwise projection_start_block.
7. Persistence is private, no-follow, checksummed, atomic temp+fsync+rename+directory-fsync; ambiguous temp state fails closed.
8. A discovered job is persisted before exposure and is never skipped by scan advancement.
9. Replay after a crash is safe and monotonic.

Transition matrix:
- No checkpoint/no job + finalized head: query start..min(start+99, head); empty success -> persist end height/hash; eligible job -> persist job, do not advance scan beyond unprocessed work; RPC/decode failure -> no mutation.
- Checkpoint + same canonical anchor + newer head: query checkpoint+1 bounded to 100; empty success -> replace checkpoint atomically; job -> persist job; failure -> retain checkpoint.
- Checkpoint at head: NoNewJob, no write.
- Checkpoint ahead of finalized head: fail FinalizedHeadBehindCheckpoint.
- Stored identity mismatch, zero/invalid fields, checksum/version mismatch, or canonical hash mismatch: fail closed.
- Existing job journal without scan checkpoint: validate job authority, use job cursor as lower bound.
- Restart/crash before rename: final checkpoint remains old; temp ambiguity fails closed.
- Restart/crash after rename: new checkpoint is canonical and resumes at height+1.
- Deadline/job availability semantics remain owned by existing record_available_for_purpose.

Canonical state shape: ScanCheckpointV1 { generation:u64, identity:EndpointIdentity(chain_id, genesis_hash, boot_nonce, protocol_bundle_hash), fork_id:B256, scanned_through_height:u64, scanned_through_block_hash:B256 }, encoded in fixed canonical binary with magic/version/checksum. File paths: exporter-v1/discovery/scan-checkpoint.v1, .tmp, and the existing discovery.lock. Compatibility: discovery.v1 unchanged; missing scan-checkpoint.v1 means legacy state and catches up safely.

Ownership: rpc_discovery owns range selection, checkpoint validation and advancement; supervisor journal module owns secure durable encoding/publication primitives; PublicOcompRpcClient remains the bounded RPC transport; caller retry loop remains unchanged.

Expected paths/hot files: bin/outbe-ocomp/src/rpc_discovery.rs and bin/outbe-ocomp/src/supervisor.rs, plus focused tests under bin/outbe-ocomp. At most two semantic passes each. Evidence: range boundary tests (1..100, 101..200), empty-scan restart persistence, exact height/hash validation, identity/checksum/temp rejection, failure non-advancement, existing job compatibility, cargo fmt/check/test for outbe-ocomp, release build and --version/SHA256.

Ordered slice: (1) durable checkpoint type/journal and tests; (2) bounded discovery integration and tests; (3) release build/artifact verification.
acceptance_criteria: Every eth_getLogs discovery request spans at most 100 finalized blocks. Empty successful ranges atomically persist a chain-bound height/hash checkpoint and restart resumes at checkpoint+1. Failed or partially processed ranges do not advance it. Existing discovery.v1 remains compatible and separate. No genesis, consensus, Mongo, node, or enclave changes. Focused tests and release outbe-ocomp build pass.
notes: Implemented a chain-bound, restart-safe finalized discovery scan checkpoint in exporter-v1/discovery/scan-checkpoint.v1. Queries are bounded to 100 finalized blocks; checkpoint advances only after successful safe processing, preserves transitional events for retry, validates canonical block hash after restart, and logs every requested range plus durable height/hash. Validation: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy -p outbe-ocomp --lib --tests -- -D warnings; cargo test -p outbe-ocomp --lib (58 passed); cargo build --release -p outbe-ocomp --bin outbe-ocomp. Release SHA256 08bd8bd78c282ac30b14a1f91c7b3c3d808843846862f7bb1a80f6d5aaa31173. Copied to /home/ubuntu/outbe-ocomp on rpc.n1..n4.testnet.outbe.net and remote hashes verified.

title: Raise initial TEE lease ceiling to 30 days for testnet
description: The testnet runs GramineDirectDev without DCAP, while automatic renewal exists only for DcapRequired. The current canonical TeePolicyV1 validator rejects maximum_lease above 604800 seconds, so a 30-day genesis cannot be accepted by the release binaries. Raise the canonical ceiling and generated initial policy to exactly 2592000 seconds, then rebuild production release artifacts without test/E2E features and regenerate the signed testnet package.

title: Reject or reseed stale Oracle genesis before testnet rollout
description: The fresh testnet release binaries stop every validator proposal task at height 0 because the packaged genesis carries the pre-multi-currency Oracle storage layout while the current runtime expects AddressPair-based registry state introduced by commit 0357ff34. The mandatory block-1 pre-execution path reads COEN/ISO-840 from current slot 10 and reverts with pair 0xcc840 not registered. Both /home/ubuntu/genesis.json and testnet_14082026.staging/genesis.json have pair_count=7 from the old schema but no current COEN/840 pair_to_index entry. This was not caused by OCOMP or SGX.
design:
Architecture freeze v5 — timestamp-only lease refresh and complete genesis-hash rebinding.

Scope: from the currently published repaired Measurement/1 genesis, construct one immutable strict base by removing only config.ocompForkInstallV1, config.metadosisStorageLayoutV1, and config.teeAttestationV1, then replace only the root timestamp with the current UTC Unix second encoded as hex. Preserve alloc and every other header/config value byte-semantically. Add a registration-only Rust helper example under bin/outbe-keygen/examples that reads the four existing OCOMP private keys and old public registrations, asserts each private key derives the registered SEC1 public key, replaces only core.genesis_hash, recomputes normalized low-S PoP, validates it through outbe-ocomp-protocol, and writes canonical registrations. Use packaged release outbe-chain SHA256 2c3cc8a684adbc55ae0766eab825a03ea0348a31162fdfdac1a970d57cca88bf to regenerate bindings, Measurement/1 install/layout/bundle, then GramineDirectDev teeAttestationV1. Refresh derived env, README, checksums, folder and archive.

Explicit non-goals: no validator EVM/BLS/P2P keys, no OCOMP key rotation, no alloc/Oracle/ValidatorSet/storage reseed, no chain ID or non-timestamp header change, no protocol timing overrides, no Rust runtime/consensus behavior change, no release binary/enclave/manifest/signature rebuild, no port/launcher change, and no remote extraction, wipe, restart, or service mutation in this slice.

Invariants: chain ID remains 54322345; all four ocomp-key-v1.hex files remain byte-identical; each new registration preserves chain ID, validator identity hash, OCOMP SEC1 public key, key epoch, and purpose bitmap and changes only genesis hash plus its PoP; validators.json and alloc remain structurally identical; genesis stripped of the three derived extensions differs from the prior stripped genesis only at root timestamp; timestamp is not in the future and is less than one hour old at publication; Measurement activation remains height 1; generated layout remains canonical; protocol bundle is generator-owned and expected byte-identical but equality must be proven; TEE mode remains GramineDirectDev; all binaries, enclave, signed manifest, signature, scripts, and validator material remain byte-identical; no test features or outbeProtocol.

Transition matrix: old timestamp + block-1 now beyond genesis+604800 -> TeeBootstrap lease subtraction reverts and block rolls back at height 0; fresh timestamp + stale old OCOMP registrations -> OCOMP generator rejects genesis-hash mismatch; fresh timestamp + rebound registrations + stale TEE policy -> startup rejects policy/genesis mismatch; fresh timestamp + exact regenerated OCOMP/layout/TEE -> startup accepts, founders admit, DKG boundary and TeeBootstrap may execute; invalid key/public-key match or PoP -> helper/generator fails before publication; replay/restart with fully wiped new-genesis runtime is safe; reuse of old Reth/consensus/OCOMP/TEE NodeHost or sealed DKG state is forbidden and must fail closed; deadline behavior requires deployment before genesis timestamp + maximum_lease, with package freshness gate below one hour.

Canonical shapes/compatibility: no wire/state type changes. OcompKeyRegistrationV1 and its codec remain authoritative; helper calls the existing protocol encoder/digest/validator and never hand-encodes OCB1. OcompForkInstallV1, GenesisMetadosisStorageLayoutV1, TeePolicyScheduleV1, and ProtocolBundleV1 retain current release codecs. Changing the root timestamp changes the canonical genesis hash; config extensions are regenerated against that single frozen hash and do not create a hash cycle.

Ownership: package assembly owns the timestamp and metadata; helper owns only existing-key registration rebinding through protocol APIs; packaged outbe-chain ocomp bindings/genesis owns identity/install/layout/bundle validation; packaged outbe-chain tee genesis owns TEE policy binding; runtime TeeRegistry owns lease enforcement; operator rollout owns mandatory state wipe and block-1 proof.

Expected paths/hot files: bin/outbe-keygen/examples/rebind_ocomp_registrations.rs (one helper implementation pass); testnet_14082026.staging/genesis.json (one generated replacement pass), ocomp-bindings.json, four registration files, protocol-bundle-v1.ocb1, RELEASE-IDENTITY.env, ocomp-worker.env, ocomp-exporter.env, README.md, SHA256SUMS, published folder/archive. No production runtime hot file.

Evidence: helper unit/CLI failure tests for key mismatch, wrong old registration, existing destination, and happy-path decoded registration; exact key SHA preservation; decoded old/new field audit; two independent regeneration runs byte-identical from the frozen base; structural genesis diff; packaged release generator identity; final dump-genesis parse; timestamp lease arithmetic green; env parity; protocol bundle equality/difference explicitly accounted; binary/enclave/signature exact comparisons; shell syntax; SHA256SUMS; archive extraction equality; two-axis review. External acceptance remains operator-approved four-host clean rollout and common finalized block 1/2 without Oracle, OCOMP, or TEE errors.

Ordered slices: (1) freeze and helper; (2) timestamp base + registrations; (3) release generator rebinding; (4) metadata/checksums/archive; (5) independent review/publication; (6) separately authorized remote wipe/rollout. Stop and re-plan on any alloc, key, validator identity, chain ID, release binary, enclave/signature, non-timestamp header/config base, or runtime production-code mutation.

Packaged release outbe-chain regenerates exact Measurement/1 install, metadosis layout, protocol bundle, and GramineDirectDev TEE policy against that hash. All derived env values, README, SHA256SUMS, folder, and extracted archive agree; binaries, enclave/manifest/signature, scripts, validators, and keys remain byte-identical; no test feature or outbeProtocol is present. title: Provision the mandatory OCOMP carrier key before validator startup
description: Fresh testnet validator startup currently reaches the embedded OCOMP ExEx without validator-N/ocomp/domain-v1/ocomp-evm-key.hex and then panics while opening the node-owned OCOMP domain. Founder provisioning intentionally creates only ocomp-key-v1.hex plus its registration; the carrier key is a separate operational EVM signer. For the current fresh genesis with no explicit OCOMP delegate, deployment must install the already-existing validator evm-key.hex as the carrier key, with strict owner/mode requirements, or explicitly provision and authorize a funded delegate. Keep genesis, founder registrations, validator key generation, harness, and production runtime behavior out of scope.
design: Deployment-only fix. Do not generate or rotate validator EVM/BLS/P2P keys. Do not alter genesis. Keep founder result-signing key ocomp-key-v1.hex distinct from the operational carrier path ocomp-evm-key.hex. In the current no-delegate topology, the carrier address must resolve to the represented validator, so install a copy of that validator's existing evm-key.hex with a single inode, owner matching the node process UID, and mode 0600. A future dedicated carrier requires explicit on-chain OCOMP delegation and funding.
acceptance_criteria: The testnet README gives an exact per-validator install command using the existing validator evm-key for the no-delegate topology; run.sh fails before launching outbe-chain with a clear actionable error when the carrier key is absent or insecure; no validator/private key is added to the archive; shell syntax/preflight regressions pass; the rebuilt tarball and SHA256SUMS contain the corrected deployment files.

2026-08-14 OCOMP incident root cause: the untracked scripts/localnet-sgx.sh assigned both the node (OUTBE_PROJECTION_MONGODB_DATABASE) and SnapshotExporter (OUTBE_OCOMP_PROJECTION_MONGODB_DATABASE) to the same _validator_ database. Each component independently owns a projection writer and MongoStorage enforces one active writer lease per database. The live node renews projection_writer_lease every 2s, so exporter open maps WriterLeaseBusy to StorageUnavailable and retries forever while remaining alive. Deterministic repro on validator-0: retry count 18604->18607 in 3s, active renewing node lease, advancing RPC head, worker idle. This is launcher misconfiguration, not Mongo outage or SGX failure. The contract was already explicit: ocomp-export.env.example says OCOMP DB must differ; E2E OcompTopology appends _ocomp (introduced in 0d2821b4/#204). E2E did not reproduce because it uses the correct separate DB; public_rpc_input_path is ignored/compile-only and has no concurrent node writer. A secondary readiness gap exists: local launcher and harness startup checks treat exporter process liveness as readiness; observe_baseline_runtime derives exporter count from supervisor count and never probes exporter progress. StorageUnavailable also erases the distinction between transient Mongo outage and permanent WriterLeaseBusy, allowing an infinite live-but-unready process.

title: Feature-gate test protocol overrides and keep production constants zero-state
description: Scope: replace EE11/state-backed constants with named scalar getters. Production/testnet builds use compile-time immutable defaults and reject config.outbeProtocol. Builds with test-protocol-overrides resolve config.outbeProtocol over defaults into a process-wide OnceLock for LocalNet/E2E acceleration. Preserve the E2E genesis-writing interface. Remove state slots, storage reads, constants CLI, runtime fallback, and production initialization state. Non-goals: genesis header/hash changes, extraData commitments, EVM state commitments, runtime mutation, public whole-record getter, or alternative override channels.
design: Corrected architecture freeze (2026-08-13, review accepted). Invariants: (1) production/testnet getters return references/scalars derived from one compile-time const DEFAULTS and cannot fail due to startup order; (2) production initialize(None) is a no-op success and initialize(Some(_)) rejects the unsupported test-only key before node launch; (3) test-protocol-overrides owns the only OnceLock, resolve-validates partial config.outbeProtocol over DEFAULTS exactly once, and named getters panic before successful initialization; (4) invalid feature overrides never initialize; (5) E2E JSON knobs and public scalar getter names remain unchanged; (6) no genesis header/hash/state mutation. Transition matrix: prod + no key -> accept/defaults/no state; prod + key present -> startup error/no runtime; feature + no key -> set defaults once; feature + valid key -> set resolved values once; feature + invalid key -> error/uninitialized; feature + repeated initialize -> AlreadyInitialized; feature getter before initialize -> panic; restart repeats the same build-specific startup transition; replay/deadlines use immutable selected values and expose no mutation. Canonical type: flat GenesisProtocolParametersV1 with all integer fields; JSON override shape remains schemaVersion/metadosis/ocomp/nodMaterialization; named scalar getters remain the runtime API. Ownership: constants crate owns defaults, validation, feature singleton and rejection; OutbeChainSpecParser owns startup invocation after TEE/OCOMP validation; OCOMP genesis helper mirrors build selection; E2E build scripts own enabling the feature. Hot files: constants src/lib.rs, outbe-chain main.rs and ocomp_genesis.rs, consumer test shims, E2E build wiring, docs. Tests: production rejection/no-state getters; feature override, invalid, repeated init and pre-init panic; OCOMP selection both modes; Metadosis/Cycle/NODFactory; workspace check/clippy; release sudo SGX no-attest metadosis-fresh-devnet with live cast WWD observation. Ordered slice: constants core/tests; startup/OCOMP integration and shim removal; build/docs; quality gates; release E2E.
acceptance_criteria: Production getters always return canonical compile-time defaults without initialization state. Production startup rejects any config.outbeProtocol key. test-protocol-overrides resolves valid partial overrides and rejects invalid values; its getters panic before initialization and are immutable afterward. Runtime consumers need no test initialization shims. OCOMP capacity matches the selected mode. Existing E2E timing knobs/genesis interface remain unchanged and all E2E node build paths enable the feature. Unit tests, workspace check, clippy, release fixture validation, live cast WWD observation, and full release sudo SGX no-attest @metadosis-fresh-devnet E2E pass.
notes: User correction (authoritative, 2026-08-13): remove load/load_from_storage and the genesis-keyed registry. The only runtime API is one explicit getter per parameter (Rust snake_case, e.g. get_metadosis_forming_period_seconds). Implementation is one process-wide OnceLock<GenesisProtocolParametersV1>, initialized exactly once from config.outbeProtocol during node startup. Consumers receive scalar values only. No public whole-structure get, no StorageHandle/BlockRuntimeContext API, no genesis-hash keying, no conflict map, no EE11/state/slots.

title: Joining validator can become ACTIVE without a private DKG share after an in-flight restart
description: At fixed production commit 96d4113d706697c9ea7ecda4552e6314d10686d1, validator_lifecycle.feature scenario 'In-flight DKG survives a joining node and enclave restart' restarts validator-4 during the Player phase. The canonical DKG outcome completes and ValidatorSet later commits active_count=5, but validator-4 logs MissingPlayerDealing and 'no private share to promote'; its keys directory contains no live DKG share. This violates docs/flows/006-validator-join-operation-and-exit.md: ACTIVE voter => canonical live DKG share; no live share => cannot sign/vote as current participant. Evidence: /tmp/outbe-e2e-main-core/validator-lifecycle/run-1786615371-1934033/scenario-5. This acceptance run must not change production code; diagnose and fix in a separate scoped branch.
design:
## Scope

Fix node-local DKG Player ingress durability for target participants and make a successful participant completion require a private Share. Preserve the existing public boundary observation path for FullNodes and non-target validators.

## Non-goals

- No ValidatorSet, EVM, genesis, TEE, OCOMP, DKG wire, boundary encoding, quorum, timeout, or cadence changes.
- No consensus-visible proof of possession or recovery after physical loss of the keys directory.
- No new E2E scenarios when the existing restart and FullNode scenarios can carry the acceptance evidence.

## Invariants

1. A local key in the frozen target participant set cannot produce a successful DkgComplete without a private Share.
2. A Player ACK means the accepted canonical DealerBundle is durably recoverable for the exact DkgCeremonyId.
3. A crash before durable persistence emits no ACK; a crash after persistence reconstructs the same Player input and ACK.
4. Duplicate identical bundles are idempotent; conflicting canonical bundle bytes are never acknowledged.
5. Player recovery state remains until the matching pending triplet and canonical boundary are promoted, then dealer and player retry state are cleared together.
6. FullNodes verify public DKG boundaries without loading participant keys, running the DKG actor, or requiring a private Share.
7. DealerOnly and NotParticipant paths remain separate from participant completion.

## Transition matrix

- Fresh target Player + ceremony start: create empty Player and empty ceremony-scoped recovery snapshot.
- Matching recovery snapshot + restart: bounded decode, deterministic dealer-order replay, and exact ACK verification before networking.
- Different ceremony snapshot: never replay it; atomically replace it when the canonical new ceremony accepts its first bundle.
- Corrupt, truncated, oversized, duplicate-dealer, or replay-inconsistent snapshot: fail closed locally.
- New valid bundle: mutate Player, atomically persist the full accepted bundle plus expected ACK, then permit ACK transmission.
- Persistence failure: return actor error and emit no ACK.
- Identical duplicate: return the persisted identical ACK without another mutation.
- Conflicting bundle: classify equivocation and emit no ACK.
- Participant finalize success: return DkgComplete with mandatory Share.
- Participant finalize failure: do not publish a successful participant boundary; retain outgoing committee and use existing retry/expiry behavior.
- Matching canonical activation: promote pending triplet and clear both recovery snapshots.
- FullNode boundary/restart: follow and verify public artifacts only; private recovery state is not opened.

## Canonical local types and compatibility

- DkgComplete becomes { output, share: Share, participants }.
- Existing DkgDealerOnlyComplete remains the non-player result.
- DkgRetryStore owns the existing unchanged dealer snapshot file and a new dkg_player_retry.hex file.
- DkgPlayerRetrySnapshotV1 contains magic/version, DkgCeremonyId, bounded entry count, and dealer-key-sorted encoded DealerPubMsg, DealerPrivMsg, and expected PlayerAck entries.
- Existing dealer snapshot encoding remains readable and unchanged. The new player file has no legacy migration requirement.
- No consensus state, block, RPC, ABI, P2P wire, or boundary bytes change.

## Ownership and expected paths

- DKG actor recovery seam: crates/blockchain/consensus/src/dkg_actor/recovery.rs, actor.rs, mod.rs.
- Activation and recovery lifecycle: crates/blockchain/engine/src/stack.rs and stack_tests.rs.
- E2E evidence only: testing/e2e-harness/src/features/restart.rs and, only if required, world/rpc.rs or features/follower.rs.
- Documentation: ADR-B-CNS-002 and flow 006.
- Hot files actor.rs, stack.rs, and restart.rs receive one implementation pass and at most one integration-correction pass.

## Verification

- RED coverage for PlayerOnly and DealerAndPlayer crash after accepted dealing, persistence failure, duplicate/equivocation, corrupt/mismatched snapshot, and activation cleanup.
- Existing signed-garbage dealer regression remains green.
- Restart scenarios 5 and 7 require hasThresholdShares=true and no new voter misses after activation.
- Existing FullNode off-grid boundary/restart scenario proves isValidator=false and no private Share requirement.
- Focused unit tests, package clippy, release build, then release SGX/no-attest E2E outside sandbox.

## Delivery

One focused PR with coherent green commits: architecture freeze; product fix plus unit tests; E2E evidence. RED tests are written and observed before production edits but committed only with the green implementation.

## Stop triggers

Stop and re-plan before any production expansion if implementation requires consensus-visible readiness, DKG or boundary wire changes, ValidatorSet changes, FullNode follower changes, a third semantic pass on a hot file, or if Commonware Player replay is not deterministic.
acceptance_criteria: A restarted joining or incumbent target validator recovers the exact ceremony Player inputs, activates only with a canonical private Share, reports hasThresholdShares=true, and does not accumulate voter misses after activation. Existing signed-garbage DKG behavior remains covered. FullNode boundary verification and restart remain shareless and green. Focused unit, engine, clippy, release build, validator restart E2E, and FullNode non-regression pass.
notes:
Three-agent classification established PRODUCT at scenario 5. A subsequent one-agent coverage audit found the exact transition is unique and must not be removed. It also found scenario 7 passes despite an analogous incumbent-validator failure: after node+enclave restart during an incomplete 4-to-5 reshare, validator-3 logs verifier mode/no private share to promote and voter misses, while the harness asserts only RPC lockstep. The product defect therefore affects both a restarted joining Player (scenario 5) and a restarted incumbent Dealer (scenario 7); ACTIVE membership can include a member without the canonical live private share. Scenario 5 evidence: /tmp/outbe-e2e-main-core/validator-lifecycle/run-1786615371-1934033/scenario-5. Scenario 7 evidence: /tmp/outbe-e2e-main-core/validator-lifecycle/run-1786615371-1934033/scenario-7.
Architecture freeze approved for one focused PR. The implementation selects durable recovery for normal process and enclave restart. It does not add consensus-visible proof of possession or change ValidatorSet, DKG wire, FullNode follower behavior, TEE, or OCOMP.
close_reason: Fixed node-local DKG Player ingress durability: participant completion now requires a private Share, restart replay is exact and persist-before-ACK, activation cleanup is atomic, and validator plus FullNode acceptance scenarios pass.

title: Keep NodeHost identity independent of node role
description: P0 lifecycle bug: persistent NodeHost identity is incorrectly derived from FullNode or Validator role. Implement one role-neutral NodeHost identity for a wiped network. Identity is created once from the persistent Reth P2P secp256k1 key, contains no role, is independent of the separately provisioned EVM, BLS and OCOMP keys, and survives every ValidatorSet lifecycle change and restart. The separate key material itself grants no role. No migration, compatibility path, activation gate, dual model or adjacent redesign.
design:
Revised architecture freeze after the three-agent deviation audit and user decision A.

Scope: one role-neutral NodeHost model for a wiped network. Every node is provisioned with its persistent Reth P2P secp256k1 identity plus separate EVM and consensus-BLS key material. These are only independent keypairs stored for the node; their presence has no role semantics. Only the existing ValidatorSet lifecycle creates validator role, status, membership, voting power, or consensus authority.

Invariants:

1. NodeIdV1, manifest, authorization, Noise/enclave identity and policy depend only on chain/genesis and persistent Reth P2P identity, never on FullNode/Validator role, EVM address, consensus BLS, or OCOMP.
2. A node running as FullNode does not pass its separate EVM/BLS material into the consensus or voting runtime. Merely storing those keys grants no protocol capability.
3. Initial registerEnclave includes one chain/genesis-bound ValidatorNodeBindingV1 between the separately provisioned EVM address and the role-neutral NodeHost hash, authorized by both EVM and NodeHost P2P signatures.
4. The same atomic registerEnclave state transition creates the NodeHost record and writes the existing validator_v1_node_hash association. There is no standalone bind API, CLI command, reverse map, or second tee join.
5. Writing validator_v1_node_hash does not assert that the address is registered in ValidatorSet. It only records an authenticated address-to-NodeHost association between independently provisioned key material.
6. registerValidator remains the sole existing owner of validator registration and consensus BLS PoP. It does not create the NodeHost association and receives no new NodeHost locator.
7. Exact replay of the same initial registration/binding is idempotent; the same EVM address bound to another NodeHost and inconsistent binding bytes reject atomically.
8. If the ordinary ValidatorSet lifecycle later assigns validator role to a node that has operated as FullNode, the node reuses the same datadir, Reth P2P key, NodeHost manifest, enclave identity, Noise key, sealed state, resident offer key, EVM key and BLS key. No TEE archive, reinitialization or second registration occurs.
9. Jail, exit, unjail, re-entry, BLS replacement permitted by ValidatorSet, renewal, enclave replacement and restart do not change NodeHost identity or the existing address-to-NodeHost association.
10. Genesis TeeBootstrapV2 carries the same embedded binding and atomically establishes genesis NodeHost records and associations.
11. Network wipe: one canonical wire/layout only; no migration, compatibility decoder, dual read/write, activation gate, reserved legacy layout, or fallback.

Transition matrix:

• provision node: create/load P2P identity plus separate EVM and BLS key material; create no on-chain role;
• initial registerEnclave: verify NodeHost evidence, EVM signature and P2P signature; atomically create NodeHost plus association; exact replay idempotent, conflict reverts;
• run as FullNode: sync/verify only; the separate EVM/BLS material remains outside the FullNode consensus/voting runtime and the association confers no role;
• registerValidator: existing EVM/BLS PoP path creates REGISTERED; pre-existing association remains unchanged;
• stake and readiness: existing REGISTERED to PENDING and confirmValidatorReady paths;
• certified boundary: existing DKG promotes PENDING to ACTIVE;
• jail/exit/re-entry/BLS change: ValidatorSet state changes only; NodeHost association and identity remain;
• renewal/replacement/restart: preserve NodeId and all committed identity/sealed artifacts;
• invalid/missing/conflicting binding: initial registration reverts without partial writes.

Canonical shapes: NodeIdV1 remains Reth-P2P-only. ValidatorNodeBindingV1 remains chain_id, genesis_hash, EVM address and node_id_hash with EVM and NodeHost signatures, but it is embedded in initial registerEnclave/bootstrap only. Remove public bindValidatorNodeHost ABI/precompile and standalone CLI command. Consensus BLS is not added to NodeId, manifest, registration intent, binding, policy, or TeeRegistry mapping.

Ownership: ValidatorSet exclusively owns role/status/stake/consensus BLS and activation. TeeRegistry owns NodeHost registration and validator_v1_node_hash. Existing tee join/onboarding owns submission of the single atomic registration. Node startup/provisioning owns local keys but does not infer any role from their existence. Bootstrap owns genesis installation.

Non-goals: DCAP/QVL redesign, NodeHost rebind/recovery, BLS rotation protocol, OCOMP changes, ValidatorSet redesign, registerValidator ABI change, new cross-module call from ValidatorSet, reverse map, standalone binding API/CLI, reshare wire cleanup, or adjacent defects.

Delivery: one focused PR. Complete RED canonical/TeeRegistry/bootstrap/provisioning/harness tests first; one coordinated production pass; at most one integration-correction pass per hot file. Expected semantic paths are primitives tee_attestation_v1.rs and tee_bootstrap_v2.rs; TeeRegistry v1.rs/v1_precompile.rs/schema/tests; existing tee join/onboarding; bootstrap handler/builder; outbe-chain provisioning/startup only where required to create or locate additional local key material; harness localnet bootstrap/joiner/role activation. Mechanical consumers and canonical artifacts only. A new invariant, unplanned production owner/path, canonical change after implementation starts, or third semantic pass triggers the three-agent deviation gate.
acceptance_criteria: Focused tests prove: role-neutral NodeId and manifest; every node is provisioned with separate EVM/BLS key material without acquiring any ValidatorSet role; initial registerEnclave atomically creates NodeHost plus authenticated address-to-NodeHost association; exact replay and conflict rollback; association confers no ValidatorSet role; FullNode runtime does not load the separate EVM/BLS material; an ordinary later registerValidator transition can use the same provisioned EVM/BLS material without changing NodeHost; certified DKG reaches ACTIVE; jail/exit/re-entry including allowed BLS replacement preserve NodeHost association; renewal/replacement/restart preserve byte-identical manifest, authorization hash, Reth P2P key, Noise identity, enclave identity, sealed state and resident offer key; bootstrap installs the same shape. No bindValidatorNodeHost public ABI/precompile/CLI, no reverse map, no second tee join or TEE archive remains. Existing ADR-S-TEE-002 and only directly affected operational docs/artifacts are updated. Release SGX/no-attest E2E runs outside sandbox through sudo with real gramine-sgx, sgx.remote_attestation=none, no DCAP/QVL and chain_id 54322345, proving FullNode sync, one role-neutral TEE registration, ordinary ValidatorSet admission/DKG/ACTIVE, restart and OCOMP participation. Final plan-vs-diff audit is clean.
notes: 2026-08-11 deviation gate: an unapproved standalone bind-validator-node-host CLI/API was detected and stopped. Three independent read-only audits confirmed that provisioning separate BLS material is valid but cannot by itself locate NodeHost from the unchanged registerValidator ABI; BLS-to-NodeHost reverse map and ValidatorSet-to-TeeRegistry dependency are rejected. User selected option A with a terminology correction: every node simply has independent additional key material; key possession has no role semantics, and role exists only in ValidatorSet. Revised design embeds the already authenticated address-to-NodeHost binding in the one initial registerEnclave transition. Production changes remain paused until this revised freeze is audited against the worktree. Permanent process rule stored as plan-deviation-three-agent-gate.
close_reason: Implemented and verified the frozen role-neutral NodeHost architecture; all focused gates and the production-shaped release SGX/no-attest FullNode-to-validator E2E pass.

title: Derive proposal timestamps from the exact parent
description: Scope: make the proposal timestamp a pure function of the exact resolved parent header and the current clock while retaining the protocol minimum advance and maximum one-block forward-drift bound. Non-goals: CE recovery, changing either drift constant, changing header/wire formats, changing genesis behavior, or refactoring unrelated finalization state. Invariants: a non-genesis proposal uses its exact parent timestamp; failed/forfeited builds cannot influence retries on the same parent; an honest proposer never emits outside the validator-accepted band; a malicious proposer cannot jump chain time beyond the existing per-block maximum; validator checks remain unchanged. Transition matrix: clock inside band -> clock value; clock behind -> parent plus minimum; clock beyond band -> parent plus maximum; failed build then retry same parent -> recompute from the same parent with no speculative local-state input; new exact parent -> recompute from that parent; genesis child -> retain existing exemption; received block outside band -> validator rejects; restart/replay -> identical calculation from parent and clock. Canonical types/compatibility: no wire, state, storage, hash, or activation changes. Ownership: application handler owns proposal calculation; node consensus owns independent validation; finalization state exposes finalized randomness/state but does not supply a synthetic parent timestamp. Expected paths/hot files: crates/blockchain/consensus/src/application/handler.rs and finalization/state.rs, plus focused handler/state tests; at most one implementation pass and one integration correction. PR slice: one independently green timestamp fix only.
acceptance_criteria: A faithful RED regression demonstrates that a failed or forfeited build cannot advance the timestamp used by a retry on the same exact parent. The built candidate remains within parent plus the existing minimum/maximum band after a long stall. Existing validator boundary tests remain green; focused consensus tests, formatting and Clippy pass. Scope audit shows no CE, wire-format, storage-layout, genesis, or drift-constant changes.
notes: Implemented tests-first on branch fix/exact-parent-timestamp. RED covered the missing exact-parent proposal seam and the absence of a read-only prev_randao access. Production now derives every non-genesis proposal timestamp from the resolved parent block, retains the existing minimum advance and maximum forward-drift bounds, and reads finalized randomness without advancing process-local timestamp state. Regression executes two forfeited build attempts on the same parent after a long wall-clock stall and proves the retry source does not move. Validation: cargo fmt --all -- --check; outbe-consensus 357/357; outbe-node timestamp protection tests 4/4 across timestamp/drift filters; cargo clippy -p outbe-consensus -p outbe-node --all-targets -- -D warnings. Scope audit: expected and actual production paths match; one implementation pass plus test integration correction; no CE, constants, wire/state format, storage, genesis, or activation changes.
close_reason: Exact-parent timestamp source implemented and protected by failed-build retry regression; focused tests and quality gates pass.

title: Join OCOMP finality with local execution without dropping exact blocks
description: Scope: repair only validator-side OcompRetentionService ordering when certified finality arrives before local canonical execution receipts. Non-goals: no OCOMP membership, JobIntent, snapshot, Metadosis, deadline, capacity, Supervisor/Worker or consensus-rule changes; no retry-ladder extension as the final design; no retention GC cleanup. Invariants: (1) every certified-finalized block is reconciled only after exact local receipts for the same hash are available; (2) a later block never substitutes for an earlier input-discovery boundary; (3) finalization callback remains constant-time and never performs provider/proof/fsync work; (4) ordered processing and idempotent exact replay survive restart/crash; (5) local retention failure cannot invalidate network consensus but must prevent unsafe local OCOMP voting; (6) queue pressure cannot silently drop a finalized identity. Current failure: H22 finality at 23:44:21, eight retries exhausted at 23:44:24, receipts appeared at 23:44:32; 241 boundaries dropped in B12 run-02.
design:
Architecture frozen for one PR slice.

Scope/non-goals: validator-side OcompRetentionService ordering only. No consensus rule, canonical wire/state, OCOMP membership, JobIntent, Metadosis, deadline, capacity, Supervisor/Worker, FullNode follower, GC, or retry-count tuning.

Invariants:
1. Certified finality may arrive before exact local execution, but reconciliation of F starts only after the executor watermark is >= F.height.
2. The exact ConsensusBlock received from certified finality remains the head item; later blocks cannot overtake it.
3. Finalization callback stays constant-time enqueue; provider/proof/fsync work remains in the node worker.
4. Transient reconciliation failure never discards the head item; retry is event-driven by execution progress with bounded backoff only as a wake fallback.
5. Candidate-bearing blocks are durably Tentative before a positive consensus vote. The existing pin journal is the durable candidate cursor; marshal is the durable certified-block authority.
6. Restart seeds the worker with marshal's recovered certified tip and the executor recovery-anchor watermark. Existing Tentative entries are reconciled idempotently by that tip or subsequent backfill notifications.
7. Queue pressure remains explicit local OCOMP unavailability and cannot invalidate consensus; unresolved Tentative entries remain non-signable.
8. Hash identity is never substituted: provider reads/proofs stay bound to the queued block hash.

Transition matrix:
- finality F, execution watermark < F.height -> retain F pending, no source read;
- execution watermark reaches F.height -> reconcile exact F once, arm exact finalized jobs, advance FIFO only on success;
- later finality while F pending -> remains queued behind F;
- duplicate finality/readiness -> idempotent replay/no-op;
- transient local error -> keep F at head, no drop;
- restart with durable Tentative and recovered marshal tip -> enqueue tip; wait for recovery anchor/backfill then reconcile;
- hash/proof corruption -> keep local OCOMP unavailable/fail closed; consensus continues;
- queue full/worker closed -> explicit hook error and warning; consensus continues.

Node-local interface/type shape: OcompRetentionExecutionHandle carrying monotonic u64 execution-finalized heights. No canonical type or storage-layout change.

Ownership:
- FinalizationActor publishes certified exact block only.
- ExecutorActor remains execution-ready authority through its existing height notification.
- engine/stack fans the execution signal to existing DKG logic and the retention execution handle, and seeds restart from marshal.
- node/ocomp/retention owns ordered join, retry, proof work, journal and snapshot arming.

Expected production paths/hot files:
- crates/blockchain/node/src/ocomp/retention.rs (one implementation pass + at most one integration correction)
- crates/blockchain/engine/src/stack.rs (one wiring pass + at most one integration correction)
No other production path without re-plan.

Tests/evidence:
- pin_lifecycle RED/GREEN: no source work before execution-ready; exact F finalizes after readiness; transient error retained; later F cannot overtake; duplicate is idempotent.
- restart characterization uses durable Tentative + recovered tip.
- focused outbe-node tests, engine compile/check, fmt/clippy for touched crates.
Single independently green PR slice.

title: B12 waits for complete committee Tribute result within one bounded window
description: Scope: correct only the B12 capacity E2E observation step. All 257 transactions were successful, but the step imposed an arbitrary 60-second per-validator observation window. Non-goals: no production retention/reconciliation changes, no capacity/concurrency/CPU changes, no protocol deadline or state/wire changes, no block-height readiness requirement, no retry of an immutable failed cold run. Invariant: after submission stops, all committee validators must expose the complete result—exactly 257 distinct canonical Tribute IDs—within one shared 300-second completion budget. The harness polls continuously and proceeds immediately when every validator is complete; it never sleeps for the full budget. Block/head heights are diagnostics only. Transition matrix: not all validators complete before deadline -> continue polling; all complete -> pass immediately; global deadline with any incomplete/wrong/duplicate set -> fail with per-validator counts and heads. Owner: testing/e2e-harness OCOMP capacity orchestration. Expected path/hot file: testing/e2e-harness/src/features/ocomp.rs, one implementation pass plus at most one integration correction. Compatibility: tests only.
design: Use one absolute Instant deadline shared by the committee. On every poll read tributes_by_day for all committee ports and classify exact length=257 plus distinct=257. Break immediately only when all ports satisfy the result. At the global 300-second deadline fail with observed count/distinct/head diagnostics per validator. title: Consolidate all E2E scenarios into complementary logical suites
description: Scope: audit all current Cucumber scenarios (53 now; the earlier baseline was 51), remove duplicated end-to-end pipelines, and reorganize retained behavior into logical suites: Tribute ingress/projection, Validator lifecycle, FullNode/follower, OCOMP/Metadosis, Governance/Update, ZeroFee, Products, and TEE onboarding. Common setup and production workflow functions are shared; a separate scenario exists only for a distinct state transition, fault, capacity boundary, security policy, or actor role. The resulting scenario count is a consequence of unique behavior, never a fixed target. Non-goals: no production protocol changes, no consensus/wire/state changes, no Final/H32 compatibility, no native DCAP acceptance run in this task, no adjacent refactor.
design: Architecture freeze. Invariants: (1) every retained requirement/evidence ID has exactly one owning scenario; (2) prerequisite steps such as fresh localnet, Tribute, JobIntent, and OCOMP processing are reusable workflow parts, not separate scenarios pretending to be acceptance; (3) the primary OCOMP scenario alone owns the complete real release SGX/no-attest Tribute -> projection -> WWD/Metadosis -> finalized JobIntent -> pin/arming/export -> Supervisor/Workers -> validator quorum plus keyless FullNode independent compute -> Lysis -> NOD -> prepared-crash/Mongo/node/process restart and exact replay; (4) validator membership changes own the 4-to-5 historical snapshot transition and reuse OCOMP workflow parts; (5) FullNode scenarios never vote and cover sync/failover/restart/promotion/off-grid boundaries; (6) faults, capacity, deadline, mutation, and security cases remain separate only where their transition conflicts with the happy path; (7) Final/H32 and pre-activation OCOMP live paths are obsolete on wipe networks. Transition groups: Tribute absent -> valid -> projected -> member-absence -> duplicate reject; Validator FullNode -> REGISTERED/PENDING -> confirm-ready -> ACTIVE -> EXITING/INACTIVE plus restart checkpoints and DKG recover/fatal branches; FullNode cold sync -> lockstep -> upstream loss/no progress -> alternate upstream/restart and warm-promotion/off-grid branches; OCOMP FORMING/LOOKBACK/OFFERING/WAITING/READY -> finalized job -> compute/vote/quorum -> NOD -> replay/restart, with capacity/deadline/fault/mutation branches; Update pending -> quorum/deadline -> scheduled -> restart -> activated, plus reject/expire/fatal branches; ZeroFee delegate -> consume -> replay/restart/paid fallback, invalid authorization, and day reset. Compatibility: test-suite-only; no canonical types change. Expected paths: testing/e2e-harness/features/*.feature, testing/e2e-harness/src/features/* only for shared orchestration and stale file-name docs, xtask OCOMP scenario tags, evidence lane/ledger/docs, harness README/tests. Hot files: src/features/ocomp.rs and evidence lane at most one implementation pass plus one integration correction. One PR slice.
acceptance_criteria: Every original scenario is mapped to one retained behavior owner, merged into a stronger scenario, or retired only when its unique invariant is already covered by a focused test. No test asserts feature filenames or scenario counts. No duplicated Final/H32, OCOMP prefix/apply/restart/delegated/fresh-devnet pipelines, capacity profile, simple admission, simple update happy path, simple ZeroFee happy path, or repeated Tribute projection boots. The primary OCOMP flow contains a keyless FullNode and real arming/export/worker calculation; no result/state injection. Existing evidence/ledger validation rejects duplicate or missing stable requirement IDs. Harness compiles; focused behavior/evidence tests pass before one release SGX/no-attest grand run.
notes:
Current mapping after the complete 53-scenario audit. Tribute suite: original 39-42 are one sequential projection/proof/duplicate flow; 7 and 8 remain separate ZK-policy branches. FullNode suite: original 2 and 3 merge into sync/chained/failover; 4 owns warm-promotion restart; 5 owns off-grid boundary restart. Validator suite: 27 owns join/active/exit; 28-33 remain six distinct restart checkpoints; 34/35 are recover/fatal DKG branches; 36 downtime slash; 37 pending readiness; original 10 is removed as a subset, while 11 owns OCOMP historical membership overlap. OCOMP suite: original 15,17,18,19,20,22 merge into one Measurement/H1 production flow with FullNode and restart; 21 owns capacity and 23 is removed duplicate; 12 worker fault, 16 incompatible supervisor, 24 deadline expiry, 25 WWD failure, 26 pre-quorum mutation remain distinct. Original 9 is retired because crates/blockchain/evm/src/precompiles.rs and crates/core/metadosis/src/tests/lysis_ingress.rs prove inactive ingress is Revert not Fatal; original 13 Final/H32 is obsolete; original 14 is retired from live E2E because crates/blockchain/node/src/ocomp/tests/fork.rs and world/ocomp startup tests prove immutable manifest mismatch before launch. Governance: 43 merges into stronger restart flow 44; 6 and 45-49 remain distinct. ZeroFee: 50 merges into stronger replay/restart flow 51; 52/53 remain distinct. Stablecoin and TEE onboarding remain unique. No permanent count/filename test was added; stable evidence IDs remain enforced by the existing ledger discovery verifier.
COMPLETE: commit 82ce04f4 consolidated 53 original scenarios into 37 complementary scenarios across 8 responsibility suites, removed duplicate Final/H32 and overlapping OCOMP pipelines, retained keyless FullNode in the production flow, and added no filename/count assertion. Release SGX grand acceptance and B12 subsequently passed.

title: Make ValidatorSet epoch activation atomic with certified BoundaryOutcome
description: P0 consensus-liveness defect found by the production-shaped release SGX/no-DCAP Tribute->Metadosis E2E. At a nominal epoch height without a certified BoundaryOutcome, generic pre-execution increments ValidatorSet.epoch_number while the active set and OCOMP snapshot remain on the prior epoch. A due OCOMP terminal request then fatals on the absent new-epoch snapshot, rolling the block back forever. Scope: make the activated ValidatorSet epoch, active membership/hash and consensus+OCOMP snapshot switch atomically only when the certified BoundaryOutcome executes. Non-goals: no OCOMP fallback, no genesis seeding, no wire/state schema change, no DKG schedule/grace change, no Metadosis lifecycle change, no adjacent cleanup.
design: Frozen invariants: (I1) epoch_number names the currently activated committee, never a merely scheduled height; (I2) epoch_number, epoch_start_{block,timestamp}, active set/hash, and incoming consensus+OCOMP snapshot advance in one checkpointed BoundaryOutcome transition; (I3) nominal boundary height without BoundaryOutcome leaves epoch and counters unchanged; (I4) block-1 genesis BoundaryOutcome bootstraps epoch 0 without increment; later BoundaryOutcome must activate exactly current+1 and records its actual block/timestamp; (I5) the existing security ordering is preserved: for a block that actually carries BoundaryOutcome, ValidatorSet and SlashIndicator per-epoch counters are reset in block-atomic pre-execution after certified-parent accounting but before receipt-visible LateFinalizeCredits, so a boundary-block absentee miss survives into the new epoch; BoundaryOutcome later advances the epoch without resetting those freshly recorded misses; no-boundary blocks perform no reset; (I6) inactive cleanup occurs exactly once in the actual BoundaryOutcome; (I7) any block/boundary validation or write failure leaves no canonical partial effects; the boundary-local checkpoint rolls back epoch/set/snapshot/cleanup and the containing block atomically rolls back staged counter reset; replay/re-execution derives only from header artifact and parent state; (I8) OCOMP continues strict current-epoch lookup. Transition matrix: H>=due/no BoundaryOutcome => no epoch/reset effects and old snapshot remains current; certified block1 boundary epoch0 => bootstrap set+snapshot epoch0; certified later boundary epoch=current+1 => pre-exec reset counters, process CPA/LateFinalize/Cycle, then BoundaryOutcome atomically advances epoch+set+snapshot and cleanup before user tx; stale/skipped/mismatched epoch => Fatal with no canonical partial effects; restart/replay => identical staged reset and activation from certified block. Owners: EVM block pre-exec owns boundary-conditioned counter-reset ordering; EVM BoundaryOutcome owns cross-module activation ordering; ValidatorSet owns separated reset versus advance primitives and set/snapshot mutation; OCOMP strict lookup is unchanged. Canonical types/compatibility: no wire/state/layout changes; hard-fork execution semantic correction for wipe deployment. Planned production paths/hot files (max two semantic passes): crates/blockchain/evm/src/executor.rs, crates/blockchain/evm/src/begin_block_precompile.rs, crates/system/validatorset/src/hooks.rs, crates/system/validatorset/src/runtime.rs; tests: evm/tests/ordering_contract.rs, existing boundary/LateFinalize ordering test, focused executor and ValidatorSet atomicity tests; docs/evidence only if current ADR states height-driven behavior. One PR slice/commit, then exact release E2E rerun. Scope correction recorded before second production pass: moving reset wholesale into the later BoundaryOutcome would erase LateFinalizeCredits misses; the split reset/advance preserves existing security semantics while keeping epoch/set/snapshot atomic.
acceptance_criteria: RED proves: at due height without BoundaryOutcome epoch/snapshot remain old and OCOMP current snapshot resolves; delayed certified boundary at the next height atomically activates current+1 and writes its OCOMP snapshot before terminal request; invalid epoch and injected failure leave prior state intact. GREEN focused ValidatorSet/EVM tests, fmt, Clippy/check. Then release rebuild outside sandbox and exact @metadosis-fresh-devnet SGX/no-DCAP full flow reaches Lysis and NOD. Actual diff must stay within frozen paths except mechanical caller/test/doc updates; any new invariant, canonical format, unplanned production path or third semantic pass stops and re-plans.
notes: Final verification: release build succeeded outside sandbox. Exact production-shaped E2E used 4 validators with real SGX/no-DCAP (`--tee sgx-no-attest`), public Tribute transactions capped at 2/block, and no direct result/state injection. Evidence: `/tmp/metadosis-boundary-retry.3ECYgm/r/run-1786286533-3079681/scenario-1`. Result: 1 feature, 1 scenario passed, 15/15 steps. The run crossed the 300-block certified boundary that previously halted, observed exactly 257 public Tributes on all validators, advanced the WWD through LOOKBACK/OFFERING/WAITING/READY, created one finalized JobIntent, ran production OCOMP domains, formed three matching validator results, atomically applied Lysis and created NOD, produced exactly 257 Tribute and NOD records, and reconstructed the certified generation from canonical history. Focused gates green: fmt; ValidatorSet full suites (79 unit +16 snapshot +2 VRF); SlashIndicator full suites; ordering_contract 2/2; delayed activation, absent-boundary, rollback, skipped-epoch and LateFinalize ordering regressions; cargo check and Clippy -D warnings for affected crates; git diff --check. Scope audit: production changes stayed in the four frozen paths; one planned implementation pass plus one integration-ordering correction in executor; no wire/state/layout, DKG schedule, Metadosis, fallback or genesis changes.

Expected paths: actor.rs production+tests only; existing @metadosis-fresh-devnet is the unmodified release-E2E acceptance.
