title: Require finalized outgoing-epoch preannounce before DKG activation
description: Confirmed production defect from SGX/no-DCAP run /tmp/outbe-e2e-follower-offgrid-fixed/run-1786195246-3325576. A late 4->5 DKG completed at height 87 (planned 60) and activated in the same supervisor iteration. No old-epoch finalized block could carry CommitteePreAnnounce(epoch=1); the first new-epoch BoundaryOutcome was certified by the unknown epoch-1 committee. The FullNode correctly failed closed at processed height 87 with repeated 'no committee verifier registered for epoch 1'. Runtime path and restart path both bypass the required authenticated handoff. This is consensus-visible and invalidates the follower-only architecture freeze; no production edit is authorized until user decision.
design:
PROPOSED AMENDED ARCHITECTURE FREEZE — PENDING EXPLICIT USER APPROVAL

Fixed point and evidence

- Branch: test/end-to-end; fixed point c95ced29771d8f83ad24d1ad7347b3e27acac7f9.
- Reproducer: /tmp/outbe-e2e-follower-offgrid-fixed/run-1786195246-3325576.
- Production-shaped profile: sudo, --tee sgx-no-attest, real SGX/Gramine, no DCAP.
- Observed: late 4→5 DKG planned for height 60 completed at height 87 and activated in the same supervisor iteration. No old-epoch finalized block carried CommitteePreAnnounce(epoch=1). The first epoch-1 BoundaryOutcome was therefore certified by an epoch the FullNode could not yet authenticate. The FullNode stopped after height 87 with “no committee verifier registered for epoch 1”.
- Three independent audits agreed that this is a consensus P0 and that the follower must not be weakened.

1. Scope

- Make DKG/validator-set rotation a two-step authenticated handoff:
  1. completed incoming material becomes durable and pre-announcable while the outgoing epoch remains active;
  2. the incoming epoch activates only after an exact CommitteePreAnnounce has been finalized by the outgoing epoch.
- Make live activation, removed-validator DealerOnly demotion, crash/restart, and verifier/follower observation use the same handoff rule.
- Preserve the existing DkgBoundaryArtifact and CommitteePreAnnounce wire forms and the existing first-new-epoch BoundaryOutcome.
- Add RED/GREEN unit/integration coverage and rerun the existing production-shaped SGX/no-DCAP off-grid follower E2E through post-boundary restart parity.

Explicit non-goals

- No change to DKG cryptography, dealer-log protocol, participant selection, ValidatorSet state, OCOMP, EVM state, genesis, TEE/DCAP, or consensus quorum.
- No follower trust fallback, self-certified boundary acceptance, epoch-by-height formula, or activation from local wall clock/process state.
- No new on-chain/wire type and no storage-layout change.
- No legacy migration for the node-local pending-boundary file: the target testnet is wiped. An old local format fails clearly instead of being guessed.
- No adjacent refactor of stack.rs, application handler, finalization actor, or follower architecture.

2. Normative terms and formulas

- planned = target.planned_activation_height.
- deadline = planned + activation_grace_blocks, using checked/saturating behavior already normative in DkgRotationParams.
- exact carrier = a canonical consensus-finalized outgoing-epoch block whose sole consensus header artifact is CommitteePreAnnounce with epoch == pending.artifact.epoch and outcome bytes == pending.artifact.outcome.
- carrier_height = height of the first exact carrier in canonical finalized history.
- activation_anchor = max(planned, carrier_height).
- A carrier at deadline is valid. A carrier after deadline is invalid/unreachable because the outgoing epoch must fail closed at deadline without an exact carrier.
- Proposed, executed-only, unfinalized, wrong-epoch, or wrong-outcome carriers never unlock activation.

3. Complete invariants

I1. DKG completion never changes active epoch, active committee, active share/polynomial, application epoch fence, or rotation anchor.
I2. Completion durably stores one immutable pending DkgBoundaryArtifact before it becomes eligible for proposal as CommitteePreAnnounce.
I3. The outgoing epoch remains the only signer/verifier epoch until both current finalized height >= planned and an exact carrier is finalized.
I4. Activation is authorized only by canonical finalized history; queued height notifications and local persisted booleans are not authority.
I5. activation_anchor = max(planned, first exact carrier height). All validator roles and restarts derive the same anchor.
I6. The next block after activation is the first incoming-epoch block and carries the exact existing BoundaryOutcome. A BoundaryOutcome cannot authenticate its own committee.
I7. The exact object persisted at completion, pre-announced by the outgoing epoch, used to build the incoming verifier, and emitted as BoundaryOutcome is byte-identical.
I8. A participant that remains/joins the target retains old active material before the carrier and promotes matching pending material only after the carrier.
I9. A removed validator executes DealerOnly duties, reconstructs and durably stores the same public pending boundary, validates/signs the outgoing preannounce, and demotes to a share-less incoming verifier only after the carrier. It never requires an incoming private share.
I10. Restart keeps active finalized boundary/material separate from pending handoff material. A pending snapshot never overwrites active recovery state.
I11. Restart before the carrier resumes the outgoing epoch with old material and restores the pending artifact for re-emission/validation. Restart after the carrier derives incoming activation from canonical history. Restart after finalized BoundaryOutcome promotes/cleans pending state normally.
I12. If local private pending material is required for an incoming participant and is absent/corrupt/mismatched, startup fails closed. DealerOnly recovery validates the public boundary but does not require a nonexistent incoming share.
I13. At deadline: exact carrier present permits activation; no exact carrier marks VRF/DKG expired and stops the validator. Completion at deadline without a previously finalized exact carrier cannot activate.
I14. Wrong/missing artifacts, provider gaps inside claimed finalized history, corrupt local snapshot, epoch/output mismatch, or impossible active/pending combinations fail closed with role/phase-specific errors.
I15. Replaying the same finalized carrier and restart recovery is idempotent. Duplicate exact preannounces do not change the first carrier or anchor.
I16. Followers continue to authenticate committees only from outgoing-epoch-finalized preannounce evidence. No production follower weakening is permitted.

4. Canonical and local type decisions

Canonical forms unchanged:

- ConsensusHeaderArtifact::CommitteePreAnnounce { epoch, outcome }.
- DkgBoundaryArtifact / BoundaryOutcome.
- DealerLog, certificates, block headers, EVM state and genesis.

Node-local pending snapshot becomes V2:

- magic = ODKGPB02;
- completed_at_height: u64 (diagnostic/recovery bound, not activation authority);
- artifact_len + exact encoded DkgBoundaryArtifact.

The misleading activated_at_height field is removed. No phase or “activated” boolean is persisted. Phase is always derived from the finalized chain.

In-memory recovered model:

- active_boundary: latest chain-finalized BoundaryOutcome and its normalized activation anchor;
- pending_handoff: validated V2 snapshot plus role derived from whether the local BLS key is in artifact outcome.players();
- finalized_carrier: optional { block_number, block_hash }, derived by scanning canonical headers no further than min(consensus_finalized_height, deadline);
- phase: AwaitingCarrier | AwaitingPlanned { carrier } | ReadyToActivate { carrier, activation_anchor } | BoundaryFinalized/cleared | Expired. This enum is internal and not serialized.

Compatibility:

- No canonical compatibility change or activation gate is required for a wiped network.
- ODKGPB01 is rejected with an explicit stale-local-format error. It is not interpreted as active state and is not silently deleted.

5. Transition matrix

| State | Event / actor | Required evidence | Effect | Error / replay / deadline |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| OutgoingActive | Freeze reached | finalized freeze-height state | Freeze target and start participant/DealerOnly ceremony | Existing retry/expiry rules remain |
| CeremonyRunning | Participant completion by deadline | canonical output and target match | Persist pending share/output (when local is incoming participant), persist V2 boundary, publish pending artifact; remain outgoing | Persistence failure is fatal; no partial activation |
| CeremonyRunning | DealerOnly completion by deadline | canonical output and target match | Build/persist exact public V2 boundary, publish it; remain outgoing with old share | No incoming share is expected |
| CeremonyRunning | Completion after deadline | none | no activation | fatal expiry |
| AwaitingCarrier | Proposal under outgoing epoch | pending artifact exists | Existing application path emits CommitteePreAnnounce | Artifact verification remains exact/fail-closed |
| AwaitingCarrier | Wrong/unfinalized/executed-only carrier | none | remain outgoing | wrong carrier rejected by block verification; unfinalized carrier ignored |
| AwaitingCarrier | Exact carrier finalizes at h <= deadline | canonical finalized header | Record first carrier. If h < planned, AwaitingPlanned; otherwise ReadyToActivate(anchor=h) | Duplicate exact carrier is idempotent |
| AwaitingCarrier | Height reaches deadline without exact carrier | canonical finalized history | mark expired; do not start incoming epoch | fatal; no self-bootstrap |
| AwaitingPlanned | finalized height reaches planned | previously finalized exact carrier | ReadyToActivate(anchor=planned) | queued/stale notifications cannot bypass evidence |
| ReadyToActivate | Participant path | exact carrier plus matching pending private material | swap to incoming material, arm outgoing fence at anchor, advance epoch, restart engine | mismatch/missing private material fatal |
| ReadyToActivate | DealerOnly path | exact carrier plus matching public boundary | drop old share, adopt incoming public output/set, advance as verifier | no private pending share required |
| IncomingAwaitingBoundary | First incoming proposal | exact pending artifact | emit BoundaryOutcome | omission/mismatch rejected by existing boundary resolver |
| IncomingAwaitingBoundary | BoundaryOutcome finalizes | exact artifact | promote participant pending state to saved active state; retire retry/snapshot; DealerOnly clears public pending snapshot | idempotent cleanup |
| Any pre-boundary phase | Restart before exact carrier | active finalized boundary + valid pending V2 + no exact finalized carrier | restore outgoing epoch/material, restore pending artifact, continue preannounce | pending must not replace active boundary |
| Any pre-boundary phase | Restart after exact carrier, before BoundaryOutcome | active finalized boundary + valid pending V2 + exact carrier | derive anchor and enter incoming epoch using participant or DealerOnly rule | canonical scan is authority |
| Any phase | Restart after matching/newer BoundaryOutcome finalized | finalized boundary | use finalized active boundary; promote/clear stale pending | existing monotonic cleanup, exact validation |
| Restart | claimed finalized range has missing/undecodable header | none | no fallback | fail closed with height |

6. Ownership map

- crates/blockchain/engine/src/stack.rs owns the handoff FSM, deadline decision, canonical finalized-carrier scan, node-local V2 snapshot, role-specific activation, restart recovery and material promotion.
- crates/blockchain/consensus/src/dkg_manager.rs remains owner of canonical DKG output reconstruction, exact pending-boundary identity, preannounce validation and BoundaryOutcome validation. Its wire/state model does not change; production edits are not expected unless RED tests prove an unavoidable missing query.
- crates/blockchain/consensus/src/application/handler.rs remains the existing emitter/verifier adapter; no production semantic edit expected.
- crates/blockchain/consensus/src/finalization/actor.rs remains the finalized-artifact notifier; no production semantic edit expected.
- crates/blockchain/consensus/src/follow/* remains the consumer of authenticated committee chaining; no production semantic edit expected, only regression evidence.
- testing/e2e-harness owns production-shaped orchestration/evidence only.

7. Expected paths and hot-file budget

Expected production path:

- crates/blockchain/engine/src/stack.rs — HOT, pass 1: final FSM/persistence/restart/DealerOnly implementation; pass 2 reserved only for integration correction.

Expected tests/evidence paths:

- crates/blockchain/engine/src/stack_tests.rs — RED transition/restart/deadline/DealerOnly tests, then GREEN.
- crates/blockchain/consensus/src/dkg_manager/tests/* and application handler tests — only if an existing exact-validation characterization is insufficient; no production expansion implied.
- crates/blockchain/consensus/src/follow/* tests — regression proving preannounce-before-boundary authentication, without follower production changes.
- testing/e2e-harness/features/follower_upstream.feature and its existing step/world support — complete the already-added SGX/no-DCAP off-grid scenario; no direct state/result injection.
- docs/reports/pretestnet-npt-e2e-2026-08-06.md — evidence row only.

Stop/re-plan triggers for this slice:

- any canonical/wire/EVM/genesis change;
- any production edit outside stack.rs unless RED evidence proves it necessary;
- weakening follower verification;
- a third semantic pass over stack.rs;
- inability to preserve old material before carrier or to recover DealerOnly without inventing a new canonical artifact.

8. Ordered PR slice

One focused P0 PR: “Require outgoing-finalized preannounce before DKG activation”.

1. Add RED pure-decision and restart classification tests covering all matrix rows.
2. Add RED participant and DealerOnly persistence/material-selection tests.
3. Implement V2 pending snapshot and canonical finalized-carrier resolver in stack.rs.
4. Route live participant and DealerOnly activation through the single resolver.
5. Route startup recovery through the same resolver; remove pending-overwrites-active behavior.
6. Run focused engine/consensus/follower tests, harness compile, then the exact sudo SGX/no-DCAP off-grid E2E.
7. Scope audit actual diff vs this map. Any required second PR is proposed, not silently added.

The PR is independently correct: before an exact carrier the old epoch continues; after it the incoming epoch is fully usable; no production path is routed through dormant/incomplete scaffolding.

9. Required RED/GREEN evidence

- late completion at/after planned remains outgoing until exact carrier finalizes;
- queued old height notification cannot activate;
- early exact carrier waits until planned;
- exact carrier at deadline activates; absent carrier at deadline expires; later carrier never unlocks;
- wrong epoch/outcome, proposed-only, executed-only and unfinalized carrier do not unlock;
- first exact duplicate-stable carrier determines anchor;
- crash after pending persistence before in-memory publish;
- crash before carrier restores old epoch/share and pending artifact;
- crash after carrier before epoch switch derives incoming epoch from chain;
- crash after switch before BoundaryOutcome;
- finalized BoundaryOutcome promotion/cleanup;
- participant missing/mismatched pending private material fails closed;
- DealerOnly completes, validates preannounce, restarts before/after carrier, and demotes without incoming share;
- follower sees preannounce_height < boundary_height and reaches exact hash/state-root parity live and after restart;
- exact production SGX/no-DCAP E2E run turns the current 8/9 result into 9/9.

Approval boundary

This design is a proposal only. No production implementation is authorized until the user explicitly approves it.

Production-shaped SGX/no-DCAP E2E reaches exact finalized hash/root parity after boundary and after restart. No self-certification or formula fallback.

title: Derive FullNode follower epochs from authenticated on-chain boundaries
description: Current FollowerEpocher still computes (height-1)/epoch_length. Validator DKG activation can be off-grid and subsequent plans accumulate from the actual activation anchor, so a FullNode can select the wrong epoch/verifier and stop following finalized blocks. The testnet observation epoch 186 at height 223123 instead of 223201 remains reproducible arithmetically in current code. Scope is follower epoch mapping/bootstrap/trust only; no EVM state, wire format, validator consensus semantics, OCOMP redesign, or unrelated cleanup.
design:
ARCHITECTURE FREEZE — P0 follower epoch drift

Scope
- FullNode follower only: replace formula-derived epoch routing and restart reconstruction with authenticated on-chain boundary observations.
- Preserve fail-closed finalization verification while supporting delayed/non-grid DKG activation and accumulated drift.
- One focused slice on the current test/end-to-end branch.

Explicit non-goals
- No validator consensus, DKG activation, EVM/state, OCOMP, wire/canonical artifact, RPC format, genesis schema, or committee cryptography changes.
- No trust in the upstream RPC: it remains a byte transport.
- No unrelated follower refactor or performance redesign.

Invariants
I1. For every admitted certified block at height H, epocher.containing(H).epoch equals finalization.round.epoch.
I2. Epoch E>=1 begins only at the exact block height carrying BoundaryOutcome(epoch=E), after its certificate verifies with the already authenticated E committee.
I3. Committee E is installed only from CommitteePreAnnounce(epoch=E) carried by a block whose certificate verifies with authenticated committee E-1. BoundaryOutcome never self-authenticates or replaces a chained committee.
I4. Formula length and activation grace are search/support bounds only; they never determine the active epoch.
I5. Exact replay of an observed boundary or committee is idempotent; conflicting epoch/height/outcome is rejected without replacing trusted state.
I6. Invalid certificate, malformed artifact, epoch jump, missing preannounce, or boundary outside the allowed window is fail-closed and cannot mutate authenticated boundary state.
I7. Restart reconstructs the same committee chain and boundary map from finalized history before marshal accepts the next height.
I8. Genesis epoch 0 remains anchored by the local genesis ValidatorSet; block 1 only proves the matching epoch-0 outcome/certificate.
I9. The follower may retry unavailable upstream data, but never substitutes a formula epoch or current committee.

Transition matrix
- AnchorMissing + valid block-1 BoundaryOutcome(0) matching genesis participants and valid epoch-0 cert -> register committee 0, record activation carrier 1, Ready(0).
- AnchorMissing + mismatch/invalid/missing carrier -> startup error, no marshal start.
- Ready(E) + valid E-certified ordinary block -> deliver; no epoch mutation.
- Ready(E) + valid E-certified CommitteePreAnnounce(E+1) -> register next committee, NextKnown(E+1); exact replay no-op.
- Ready/NextKnown + invalid or non-sequential preannounce -> reject/drop, no trusted-state replacement.
- NextKnown(E+1) + valid E+1-certified BoundaryOutcome(E+1) at H within bound -> observe H as exact first height, then deliver with epocher epoch E+1.
- Ready(E) + E+1 boundary without authenticated preannounce -> drop/retry; never self-register.
- Any + forged/mismatched cert, payload, height, artifact epoch, conflicting boundary, or beyond-grace boundary -> reject/fail closed; no boundary mutation.
- Restart at recovered H -> use recovered certificate epoch only as an untrusted target hint; for every epoch reconstruct prior-certified preannounce then verify its boundary, record exact heights, finally verify H. Missing history -> startup error.
- Live out-of-order resolver fetch -> a boundary arriving before its preannounce is dropped and retried by marshal; no formula fallback.
- Deadline behavior -> not applicable; this slice has no wall-clock or OCOMP deadline transition.

Canonical types and compatibility
- ConsensusHeaderArtifact, DkgBoundaryArtifact, finalization bytes, genesis, state layout, and RPC stay byte-for-byte unchanged.
- FollowerEpocher becomes a process-local shared observed-boundary registry; no persisted or consensus-visible type is introduced.
- epoch_length_blocks and dkgActivationGraceBlocks are read from the same genesis resolver used by validator rotation and only bound discovery.

Ownership
- follow/epocher.rs owns height-to-observed-epoch mapping and monotonic/idempotent boundary rules.
- follow/mod.rs owns authenticated committee-chain transitions.
- follow/engine.rs owns startup reconstruction from finalized history.
- follow/resolver.rs owns live certificate/artifact authentication before any follower mutation and delivery.
- follow/driver.rs owns only bounded hinting/retry; it does not predict/register epochs.
- engine/src/stack.rs owns production construction with the shared genesis length/grace values.

Expected production paths and hot files
- crates/blockchain/consensus/src/follow/epocher.rs: pass 1 observed registry; pass 2 integration correction only.
- crates/blockchain/consensus/src/follow/mod.rs: pass 1 authenticated transition helper; pass 2 integration correction only.
- crates/blockchain/consensus/src/follow/engine.rs: pass 1 restart reconstruction; pass 2 integration correction only.
- crates/blockchain/consensus/src/follow/resolver.rs: pass 1 live authentication/order; pass 2 integration correction only.
- crates/blockchain/consensus/src/follow/driver.rs: pass 1 remove formula preregistration and bound hints; pass 2 integration correction only.
- crates/blockchain/engine/src/stack.rs: one construction pass.
No other production path is approved without stop/re-plan.

Test-first evidence
- RED unit: delayed non-grid activation, accumulated drift, exact replay and conflicting observation.
- RED restart: middle-of-drifted-epoch reconstruction bounded by epoch_length+activation_grace.
- RED trust: preannounce trap/self-certification rejection and forged fetched block leaves boundary/committee unchanged.

title: Make embedded OCOMP ExEx crash-restart checkpoint recovery-safe
description: Production-shaped fresh-devnet crash restart proved that the independently fsynced OCOMP ExEx checkpoint can legitimately be one finalized block ahead of Reth LastFinalizedBlock. After exact canonical validation of a loaded checkpoint C, enter StartupRecovery. provider finalized < C waits without scanning, rewinding, deleting or rewriting C and keeps readiness CatchingUp. target == C requires exact hash and enters Running; target > C replays normally. Any later regression remains Fatal. Fatal handoff sends the existing node-exit signal and keeps the ExEx future pending until teardown instead of returning Ok. Production hot file: bin/outbe-chain/src/ocomp_exex.rs; tests first.

title: Remove node-local Lysis gate from canonical quorum activation
description: Correct the OCOMP authority and FullNode verification model before completing the production E2E. A matching ResultVoteV1 quorum from the job-pinned ACTIVE ValidatorSet is the canonical Lysis decision and is applied deterministically. Every FullNode independently computes the same finalized job and compares its exact result with the canonical quorum result. A mismatch does not invalidate the canonical block for other nodes, but is a fatal local data-integrity failure: the affected FullNode logs both bindings/digests and stops.
design: ARCHITECTURE FREEZE V2 2026-08-07. One embedded OCOMP Supervisor ExEx serves Validator and FullNode. Node owns the existing ZeroMQ Worker endpoint; wire format is unchanged. Validator uses existing compute, sign-once and ResultVote submission semantics. FullNode has no vote keys, computes independently, compares against the finalized q-forming ResultVote, and on mismatch or proven local corruption persists evidence and stops only itself. At deadline D without local result, FullNode does not fatal: an optional OCOMP readiness handle in follower ExecutorActor remains at D-1 and blocks new_payload for D+1 until exact local result or finalized NoQuorum. ExEx FinishedHeight is checkpoint/pruning only. A durable contiguous {height,block_hash} watermark is fsynced after all prior jobs are terminal and used with set_notifications_with_head on restart. Multiple live jobs are independent per JobId; new jobs never cancel old jobs; state is reconstructed by canonical scan plus existing retention/CAS, with no new durable scheduler or replay engine. Finalized NoQuorum closes Computing, WaitAtDeadline, or LocalReady and releases the barrier without Lysis/NOD. Canonical result is recovered from the finalized successful q-forming ResultVote transaction and bound to LysisActivated/OcompCompletedBinding; NOD roots/counts are checked against ActiveGeneration. No wire/state/layout, consensus, membership, quorum, deadline, jail, Worker protocol, capacity, or GC change.
acceptance_criteria: Validator Node-owned ZeroMQ and embedded ExEx produce and submit the existing ResultVote without semantic change. FullNode loads no vote keys, computes the same finalized JobIntent, waits locally at deadline without advancing D+1, resumes after a late exact result, closes on finalized NoQuorum, and stops only itself on exact mismatch or unrecoverable local corruption. Two live JobIds progress independently. Durable checkpoint plus canonical backfill recover unresolved jobs and immutable NOD artifacts after restart. No standalone Supervisor remains in production wrappers. Focused tests, compile, formatting, Clippy, OCOMP gates and production-shaped E2E pass; no wire/state/layout changes.
notes: 2026-08-07 implementation checkpoint: consensus/EVM local-result authority seam removed; focused Metadosis q-forming test passes and cargo check -p outbe-evm -p outbe-node -p outbe-chain passes. New stop/re-plan trigger: current HTTP/ZMQ production Supervisor computes CompletedSupervisorJobV1 in bin/outbe-ocomp, but LocalLysisResultStore has no production writer and the node has no canonical-result observer. Therefore mandatory FullNode exact/mismatch/fatal semantics cannot be truthfully implemented by merely retaining the old store. Three independent audits launched for minimal runtime seam, UID/deployment boundary, liveness transition matrix and data ownership. No further FullNode production edits until reconciled.
close_reason: All implementation children are closed and the parent acceptance is covered by merged embedded OCOMP, restart/replay, FullNode parity and production-shaped Tribute→NOD evidence.

title: Add immutable genesis-backed chain constants for fast production-shaped E2E
description: Create a dedicated crates/blockchain/constants crate as the sole owner of genesis-configurable protocol timing. Fresh genesis resolves optional config.outbeProtocol fields against canonical defaults, validates them, materializes one immutable ProtocolConstantsV1 record in reserved genesis storage before OCOMP registrations bind genesis_hash, and exposes typed reads to all consumers. LocalNet uses short genesis values so Tribute -> Metadosis -> OCOMP -> Lysis -> NOD runs in minutes without test-only runtime overrides.
design: ARCHITECTURE FREEZE. Scope: seven immutable fields: Metadosis forming/lookback/offering/waiting/bootstrap-duration/advance-interval in seconds and OCOMP compute-vote window in blocks. JSON omissions use defaults once during genesis construction; unknown/zero/overflow/out-of-cap values fail generation. Canonical state: ProtocolConstantsV1 { schema_version=1, six Metadosis timing u64 values, one OCOMP window u64, parameters_hash, installed }. Dedicated system account 0x...EE11, fixed append-only slots, marker code, no public precompile and no post-genesis write API. Runtime API returns Arc<ProtocolConstantsV1>; callers cannot observe whether a value was explicit or default. Cache is immutable and keyed by nonzero genesis_hash; first read validates all slots/hash, later reads avoid state; zero-genesis test contexts do not share global cache. Missing/corrupt runtime record is fatal, never default fallback. Genesis ordering: base/prefund -> seed_genesis -> Rust constants materialization -> OCOMP bindings/keygen/install -> TEE install, so constants are committed by genesis_hash and do not create the OCOMP registration fixed point. seed_genesis.py supports the outbeProtocol input/profile but never duplicates slot ordinals. Metadosis receives durations from the crate and persists absolute WWD boundaries; Cycle derives the WWD advancement trigger period from the resolved advance interval while daily WWD creation/emission stays UTC-midnight-owned; OCOMP genesis writes the resolved vote window into CapacityProfile/OcompRequestProfile and each job continues pinning its actual deadline. Configurable values may shorten but not exceed frozen production maxima in this E2E slice; fixed codec/crypto/storage/domain/capacity constants are non-goals. Fresh wipe: no migration, legacy fallback or activation gate. Transition matrix: absent JSON field -> default then full record; valid override -> validated full record; invalid override -> no output; first runtime read -> validate/cache; repeated read/restart/replay -> same genesis-bound value; missing/corrupt record -> fatal; reorg -> no effect because genesis state immutable; runtime write attempt -> no API; LocalNet fresh WWD -> block-1 schedule, periodic advance, offering/ready; OCOMP job -> configured block deadline. Owners: outbe-chain-constants owns defaults/JSON/storage/hash/cache; genesis tooling owns ordering; Metadosis owns phase transitions; Cycle owns trigger dispatch; OCOMP profile owns per-job pinned deadline; harness owns fast values. Expected paths: Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock; crates/blockchain/constants/**; bin/outbe-chain/src/{main,constants_genesis,ocomp_genesis}.rs; crates/core/metadosis/src/{constants,lifecycle,state,commit,ocomp/profile,ocomp/transitions}.rs plus focused tests; crates/system/cycle/src/{triggers,runtime}.rs plus tests; OCOMP protocol capacity/profile callers and xtask fixtures only where the default is currently duplicated; scripts/{seed_genesis,prepare_network}.py and tests; testing/e2e-harness localnet bootstrap/config/features; existing genesis/Metadosis/Cycle/OCOMP ADRs, flow docs and new docs/genesis-protocol-constants.md. Hot files limited to two semantic passes: metadosis lifecycle.rs/state.rs, cycle triggers.rs/runtime.rs, outbe-chain ocomp_genesis.rs, localnet bootstrap.rs, seed_genesis.py. One PR slice on existing test/end-to-end branch, with commits for crate/genesis, consumers, and LocalNet/docs; no adjacent cleanup.
acceptance_criteria: RED/GREEN tests prove explicit override, per-field default, unknown/invalid rejection, stable hash and slot roundtrip; constants genesis changes genesis_hash before OCOMP bindings and OCOMP extension leaves it unchanged; cache reads state once per genesis and cannot cross-contaminate identities; all production consumers obtain resolved values only through outbe-chain-constants with no is_devnet/is_testnet timing branch or duplicated 50h/502h/12h/1800 literals; LocalNet seeding no longer installs the far-future OFFERING WWD bypass and a fresh block-1 WWD advances under short genesis timings; OCOMP JobIntent uses configured deadline and default remains 1800; canonical tests verify absent JSON preserves production defaults; seed_genesis.py, prepare_network.py and harness order constants before OCOMP registration; documentation lists path/type/unit/default/range/consumer/consensus effect and LocalNet/production examples. Focused tests, workspace check, formatting, Clippy, machete, OCOMP registry/shape/capacity/fixture gates and production-shaped LocalNet Tribute->Metadosis->OCOMP->Lysis->NOD pass outside sandbox.
notes:
2026-08-07 integration corrections: (1) direct outbe-ocomp-protocol -> outbe-chain-constants dependency is forbidden because outbe-primitives already depends on ocomp-protocol and constants depends on primitives. Frozen ownership remains: genesis defaults live only in outbe-chain-constants; ocomp-protocol remains pure and upper installers import constants. (2) Initial WWD timing was initially modeled from the raw UTC date start; runtime E2E below proved an unresolved UTC-vs-UTC+14 semantic split that now requires an explicit user decision before edits.

2026-08-07 runtime evidence: canonical LocalNet bootstrapped and started at /tmp/outbe-testnet; 4 validators, 4 supervisors, 4/4 workers connected, heights advanced uniformly. The first mise tribute-offer used its managed-stack defaults (RPC 9545) and did not exercise protocol. One independent architecture review classifies raw UTC as a deliberate first-midnight accounting bridge and warns that production change also affects first Cycle/day-limit formation; it recommends keeping production and deriving LocalNet seed-day from exact genesis UTC timestamp/event. Both paths are small in immediate files but choose different consensus semantics. No edits permitted until user decides. 2026-08-07 user decision: Variant A approved. The block-1 initial WorldwideDay must use the same canonical UTC+14 WorldwideDay::from_timestamp semantics as all subsequent creation. The raw-UTC first-day special case is rejected. Before production edits: add regressions on both sides of the 10:00 UTC boundary, exact block-1 key/event/deadlines, and first-midnight Cycle behavior. Minimal ownership/file map remains Metadosis lifecycle plus LocalNet bootstrap calculation and directly affected tests/docs only; any broader consensus path triggers re-plan.
2026-08-07 Variant A implemented test-first. RED reproduced at exactly 10:00 UTC: block-1 path created raw UTC 20260302 instead of canonical UTC+14 20260303. Minimal fix delegates initial creation to the existing validated canonical create_worldwide_day_if_needed path; LocalNet forming period now derives the same canonical WWD on both sides of the boundary. First-midnight Cycle regression confirms canonical genesis WWD is retained while the separate daily-emission path explicitly materializes only the settled previous UTC accounting day. All agree burst=8 must remain and the network must demonstrate backpressure across blocks; OFFERING must be long enough for all 257 offers. This is a new liveness invariant and a consensus-or-genesis boundary decision, so the AGENTS architecture-freeze stop trigger applies. No production edits made; awaiting user decision between production gas repricing and a fresh-SGX-only block envelope.

title: Simplify OCOMP finalized discovery and derive vote identity from existing signer mapping
description: Correct the OCOMP production path before testnet wipe. A Supervisor discovers finalized OffchainJobRequested, reads the matching finalized OcompJobRecord and JobIntent from local node RPC, computes Lysis, signs one OCOMP-key-bound vote and submits it. Historical ValidatorSet reconstruction and eth_getProof are not Supervisor responsibilities. Consensus state owns the pinned ACTIVE ValidatorSet snapshot used for vote validation, quorum and deadline accountability. Remove snapshot-relative OCOMP_VALIDATOR_INDEX from vote identity and use the existing OCOMP key/delegate associations. Deliver with the production-shaped SGX E2E work in branch test/end-to-end as one testnet-readiness PR.
design: Scope: one testnet-readiness PR on branch test/end-to-end. OffchainJobRequested remains an intentId pointer; discovery reads the matching OcompJobRecord and JobIntent from finalized local node state, never reconstructing historical ValidatorSet or FinalizedIntentProof. Snapshot Exporter reuses the durable discovery record. Exact Fidelity/Oracle openings remain proof-bearing inputs but are built by a purpose-bound node RPC from the local historical state provider; Supervisor does not call eth_getProof. ResultVoteV1, ResultVotePrefixV1, ResultVoteSigningSubjectV1 and SignOnceRecordV1 replace snapshot-relative validator_index with ocomp_key_hash derived from the signing OCOMP public key. Existing ValidatorSet ocomp_key_hash_to_validator resolves inner cryptographic identity to validator; existing validator_by_role_delegate resolves the outer OCOMP EVM carrier signer. Metadosis scans the already-pinned bounded historical snapshot for the resolved validator/key, derives the internal bitmap/accountability slot, and verifies the signature against that historical member key. No ValidatorSet storage or layout change is allowed. OCOMP_VALIDATOR_INDEX remains only a deployment-directory ordinal for base/validator-X and is forbidden as vote identity. Scope excludes membership, quorum, deadline, jail, Lysis, CE, DCAP and unrelated lifecycle changes. Invariants: finalized event is discovery pointer; state JobIntent is calculation authority; snapshot is consensus-owned and never enumerated by Supervisor; event/job mismatch or missing/non-open/expired state yields retry or abstention without fallback; inner OCOMP signature remains result authority while EVM signer is transport/fee authorization; first valid key-bound vote records the derived slot; exact retry, equivocation, late-vote and restart semantics stay unchanged; FullNode computes without signing. Owners: ocomp-protocol owns wire/signing; ValidatorSet owns existing registration/delegate associations; Metadosis owns historical resolution and accountability; outbe RPC owns purpose-bound openings; discovery/exporter own finalized state consumption; Supervisor owns Lysis/sign-once/submission. Expected production paths: crates/system/ocomp-protocol/src/{vote,activation}.rs and fixtures; crates/core/metadosis/src/ocomp/vote.rs; txpool and EVM carrier authorization; crates/blockchain/rpc/src/{api,server}.rs plus node RPC wiring if required; bin/outbe-ocomp/src/{rpc_discovery,rpc_input_exporter,public_rpc,result_attestation,sign_once,main}.rs; ocomp.sh, ocomp.env.example, focused docs and E2E harness. ValidatorSet schema/state are explicitly excluded unless evidence invalidates an existing association. Hot files are protocol vote.rs, Metadosis vote.rs, outbe-ocomp main.rs and rpc_input_exporter.rs, each limited to implementation and one integration-correction pass. Ordered slices inside the one PR: red tests and key-bound vote; red tests and finalized local RPC discovery/openings; deployment/harness/docs and real SGX E2E; scope audit and gates.
acceptance_criteria: No Supervisor or SnapshotExporter eth_getProof call or historical ValidatorSet reconstruction. No vote, sign-once or runtime identity uses OCOMP_VALIDATOR_INDEX; any remaining use is deployment-directory ordinal only. Vote carries OCOMP key hash, existing key-hash reverse reservation identifies the validator, existing OCOMP delegate reverse mapping authorizes the EVM carrier, and the pinned snapshot is scanned to derive the internal slot and historical verification key. No new ValidatorSet storage slot or layout change. Finalized event resolves matching VotingOpen JobIntent through local RPC; purpose-bound node RPC returns exact Fidelity/Oracle openings. Existing quorum, deadline, jail-only-current-ACTIVE, replay and restart semantics pass. SGX-no-attest E2E proves Tribute through Supervisor/Workers and signed votes to Lysis/NOD plus FullNode computation. Formatting, builds, focused/workspace tests, Clippy and registry/fixture/shape gates pass; docs match implementation.
notes: User correction 2026-08-07: no per-snapshot address-to-index reverse storage. The EVM carrier signer is already associated with a validator by ValidatorSet OCOMP role delegation; the immutable key_epoch=1 registration also reserves OCOMP key hash to validator across exit/cleanup. Result vote drops snapshot-relative validator_index. Pool/executor resolve the outer signer to validator using the existing mapping; Metadosis finds that validator in the pinned historical snapshot, verifies the historical OCOMP key/signature, and derives the accountability position. The attempted slot-59 implementation was removed before further production work.

title: Make OCOMP historical proof window work by default
description: PW-01 production blocker. OCOMP Supervisor and SnapshotExporter prove the exact finalized JobIntent request block with eth_getProof, while Reth defaults rpc.eth-proof-window to zero, which permits only the tip. Scope: derive one bounded minimum from the existing OCOMP maximum job lifetime, apply it as the outbe-chain RPC default, reject an explicitly lower value, add focused regression tests, rerun the production-shaped SGX-no-attest OCOMP E2E, and update authoritative/operator docs. Non-goals: no consensus, wire, state, finality, discovery, RPC protocol, harness-only override, unlimited proof window, or adjacent OCOMP lifecycle changes.
design: Invariant: every live OCOMP job remains independently provable at its exact request block through its maximum lifetime. Required window = awaiting-finality deadline 64 + minimum finality depth 4 + compute/vote window 1800 = 1868. Owner: node OCOMP fork/startup derives the requirement; outbe-chain startup owns the effective RPC default and fail-closed validation. Transition matrix: absent CLI value -> effective 1868; explicit 1868 -> accept; explicit greater -> preserve and accept; explicit below -> startup error before node launch; non-OCOMP chain behavior must remain unchanged if reachable. Hot files: crates/blockchain/node/src/ocomp/fork.rs and bin/outbe-chain/src/main.rs, at most implementation plus integration-correction passes. Tests first; existing production E2E must pass without a harness proof-window flag.
acceptance_criteria: Focused tests prove the derived 1868 value, Outbe default application, preservation of larger explicit values and rejection of smaller explicit values. Shared E2E node arguments permanently include --rpc.eth-proof-window 1868 for every node role. Production-shaped SGX-no-attest OCOMP scenario reaches Worker votes, Lysis and NOD. Documentation states the bounded window and RPC exposure controls. Diff contains no consensus/wire/state changes.
notes: User correction accepted: shared E2E node launch permanently passes --rpc.eth-proof-window 1868 for validator, FullNode, follower and joiner testability. This is additional to, not a replacement for, the outbe-chain production default and fail-closed validation. Production default is proven by focused parser/startup tests; production-shaped E2E proves the runtime pipeline with the permanent explicit E2E flag.

title: Restore production SGX-no-attest GramineDirectDev network profile
description: Regression introduced by f84f1576: DCAP integration coupled the on-chain AttestationMode to the local enclave session type. Before that commit, the documented localnet ran the production enclave under gramine-sgx with sgx.remote_attestation=none and EGETKEY sealing. Current code forces GramineDirectDev to the legacy Development client, rejects Production+GramineDirectDev in OST3, makes production evidence generation always acquire DCAP collateral, and makes the test launcher enable DCAP whenever SGX devices exist. Restore the explicit profile Production NodeHost session + real SGX + SgxNoAttest + GramineDirectDev evidence, while preserving the separate mock/development profile and DcapRequired fail-closed behavior.
design: SCOPE: decouple local TEE session profile from consensus attestation policy; add an explicit local production-NodeHost selection usable with GramineDirectDev; permit the production enclave to sign GramineDirectDev registration evidence only when its locally detected Gramine attestation type is SgxNoAttest; make the Gramine test launcher select remote_attestation explicitly; add an SGX-no-attest harness mode and document/run it. NON-GOALS: no new consensus AttestationMode or wire/state field; no DCAP verifier/collateral change; no native-DCAP acceptance; no software gramine-direct fallback for the SGX profile; no remote-session, renewal, upgrade, OCOMP protocol, capacity-model or release-artifact redesign; keep mock development localnet supported. INVARIANTS: (1) DcapRequired always uses a production NodeHost session and generates canonical DCAP quote/collateral; (2) DcapRequired+Development is startup-fatal; (3) GramineDirectDev evidence never claims SGX/DCAP; (4) explicit SGX-no-attest profile must use production binary, gramine-sgx, SGX device, EGETKEY sealing and production NodeHost session; (5) production dev-evidence signing is allowed only when enclave-local AttestationType is SgxNoAttest; None/Dcap/Epid/Unavailable deny it; (6) no automatic fallback between production and development sessions; (7) mock/dev profile remains a separately explicit GramineDirectDev path; (8) restart restores the same sealed identity/manifest and reconnects through the same session profile. TRANSITION MATRIX: DcapRequired+policy-default/production+DCAP => NodeHost init/reconnect, DCAP evidence; DcapRequired+development => reject before execution; GramineDirectDev+development+mock/gramine-direct => existing dev evidence; GramineDirectDev+production+SgxNoAttest => NodeHost init/reconnect, existing GramineDirectDev evidence, no quote/collateral; GramineDirectDev+production+None/Dcap/Epid/Unavailable => enclave refuses dev-evidence signing and startup fails; late/replay/deadline semantics unchanged; restart uses sealed NodeHost manifest and identity. CANONICAL TYPES: AttestationEvidenceV1, RegistrationIntentV1, TeePolicyV1, RuntimeEnclaveClient and all consensus storage/wire encodings remain byte-identical. Only a local CLI/session enum and harness mode are added. OWNERS: engine args resolves policy+local session; outbe-chain and engine stack create the chosen client consistently; tee_bootstrap owns evidence selection; enclave initialization owns local SgxNoAttest capability; enclave transport signs the existing dev intent; harness owns runtime/device/manifest selection; docs own operator claims. EXPECTED PRODUCTION PATHS: crates/blockchain/engine/src/args.rs, bin/outbe-chain/src/main.rs, crates/blockchain/engine/src/stack.rs, crates/blockchain/engine/src/tee_bootstrap.rs, crates/system/tee/src/client.rs, crates/system/tee/src/protocol.rs comments, bin/outbe-tee-enclave/src/initialization.rs, bin/outbe-tee-enclave/src/transport.rs. HOT FILES: stack.rs, tee_bootstrap.rs, main.rs, initialization.rs, transport.rs, proc.rs each receive one planned semantic pass and at most one integration correction. TEST-FIRST VERTICAL SLICES: A local session-policy resolution matrix; B authenticated production transport signs exact GramineDirectDev intent only with injected SgxNoAttest capability and rejects DCAP/None; C bootstrap emits existing dev evidence from AuthorizedEnclaveClient without collateral; D harness command proves gramine-sgx+remote_attestation=none+production session with no fallback; E cold localnet startup/restart and OCOMP reachability. title: Fail fast on residual pre-marshal startup live-join recovery
description: A normal synchronized FullNode promotion already selects VerifierOnly and reaches PENDING -> DKG -> ACTIVE. The residual production defect is an existing-chain validator with missing, stale, incomplete, or mismatched threshold material: obtain_threshold_material selects StartupLiveJoinRequired, and run_consensus_stack then waits for future height/boundary before marshal and executor start. Replace this impossible pre-marshal recovery with an immediate diagnostic startup error.
design: ARCHITECTURE FREEZE. Scope: remove the residual pre-marshal StartupLiveJoinRequired wait and make every selection of that fallback fail fast. Non-goals: no stack actor reordering, no new share-recovery protocol, no changes to DKG/BoundaryOutcome consensus semantics, wire/state types, normal FullNode promotion, or runtime reshare. Invariants: (1) startup before marshal never waits for a future execution/finality height; (2) synchronized shareless joiners continue as VerifierOnly; (3) valid current material remains Ready; (4) fresh proven genesis alone may run initial DKG; (5) missing/stale signer material produces an explicit operator-recoverable error. Transition matrix: existing chain + current valid material -> Ready; existing chain + public polynomial/output and no share -> VerifierOnly; existing chain + missing/stale/incomplete/mismatched material -> immediate error, no replay/wait; fresh proven genesis + local founder -> InitialGenesisDkg. Canonical types/compatibility: unchanged. Ownership: engine startup threshold-material selection. Expected production path/hot file: crates/blockchain/engine/src/stack.rs, at most implementation plus one integration correction. Tests: crates/blockchain/engine/src/stack_tests.rs test-first. Documentation: correct ADR-B-CNS-002 recovery row if needed. One PR slice only.
acceptance_criteria: Existing-chain startup with missing/stale/incomplete threshold material fails immediately with an actionable verifier-material recovery instruction and never enters a future-height wait; normal VerifierOnly promotion, valid Ready material, and initial genesis DKG behavior remain unchanged; focused regression tests and engine quality gates pass.
notes: Implemented on branch fix/ohz4-startup-live-join-fail-fast. Removed ThresholdMaterial::StartupLiveJoinRequired, its pre-marshal run_startup_live_join_reshare call/path, and obsolete recovery-only helpers. Existing-chain missing/stale material now returns an actionable immediate error directing restart with current public polynomial + DKG output and no signing share; VerifierOnly/Ready/genesis paths are unchanged. Test-first evidence: focused test failed before implementation (missing helper), then passed. Final evidence: cargo test -p outbe-engine --lib (172 passed), cargo clippy -p outbe-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo fmt --all -- --check, git diff --check. Scope audit: expected production path stack.rs only; touched stack.rs once semantically, stack_tests.rs, existing ADR and operator doc; no wire/state/consensus format or actor-order changes.

title: P7: enforce immutable OCOMP key_epoch 1 across validator re-entry
description: A historical live attempt pins the OCOMP public key that was active when its ValidatorSet snapshot was created. Current confirm-ready replacement semantics can install a different key while that attempt remains open; the node then has only the new secret and cannot sign the old attempt, so a validator that is ACTIVE again can be jailed for a vote it can no longer produce. Key rotation, expiry and recovery are explicitly outside this goal.
design: V1 permanently pins one OCOMP public key (key_epoch=1) to the validator address. First admission creates the forward pin and reverse reservation. Re-entry requires the same public key; a different key is rejected. Exact replay remains allowed. If a BLS change alters validator identity, confirm-ready accepts a new PoP/registration for that new identity only when the OCOMP public key is unchanged; readiness and registration payload may refresh, but the key pin and reverse reservation are never released by ordinary exit/re-entry cleanup. Loss or rotation requires a future explicit protocol outside scope.
acceptance_criteria: RED tests show replacement with a different OCOMP key is currently possible and strands an old live attempt. GREEN: first registration pins key_epoch 1; exact replay and same-key re-entry succeed; BLS-identity refresh with the same OCOMP key and valid new PoP succeeds; different-key replacement fails atomically; reverse reservation is never released or squattable during exit/re-entry; historical attempts remain signable with the same key; loss/rotation has no hidden fallback.

title: P7: make deadline sanction ACTIVE-only and non-fatal
description: A pinned participant was ACTIVE when the attempt started but can legitimately have a different current ValidatorSet status at the exclusive deadline. For each missing participant at deadline, read only its current status: ACTIVE transitions to JAILED exactly once; JAILED, PENDING, REGISTERED, EXITING, UNBONDING, INACTIVE and EXITED receive no ValidatorSet mutation. Every missing participant remains recorded in accountability. Do not call a generic transition whose unsupported statuses can Revert/Fatal.

title: P7: keep quorum-complete OCOMP jobs live until deadline
description: On-chain quorum applies the canonical result but deliberately leaves empty accountability slots open until the exclusive 1800-block deadline. design: Separate result completion from response-window closure. Completed/Conflicted jobs remain retained, exported, discoverable, attestable and signable for pinned participants until the exclusive deadline. Preserve the already-applied canonical result. Only the deterministic deadline close transitions the node-facing job lifecycle to terminal. Restart/reconciliation must recover this state exactly, including jobs whose quorum was reached before restart.

GREEN: quorum does not terminalize node retention; List/Get/export/sign-once remain available until deadline; restart restores the same job and exact-retry semantics; all remaining timely votes update accountability without changing the canonical result; deadline closure finally terminalizes the job; no timely validator is jailed merely because quorum formed earlier.

title: P10: route validator-authenticated OCOMP votes through the system execution lane
description:
## Goal

Implement the agreed OCOMP vote carrier now. A validator submits its cryptographically authenticated ResultVoteV1 through one canonical replay-visible system transaction with visible gas_limit=30,000.

## Required semantics

Classify the OCOMP system carrier before ordinary Ethereum intrinsic-gas rejection. Charge no validator fee and do not consume or crowd out the 30M user-transaction gas lane. Decode, historical-snapshot authorization, signature verification, accountability writes, q-forming application and terminal state execute against a separate deterministic internal system-work budget. Preserve canonical proposer/import/historical replay agreement and exact signed bytes across retries.

## Scope

This task is the narrow OCOMP implementation. A generic framework for unrelated future system transaction classes is deferred. Remove the stale 9M fixture and former 30M vote-envelope assumptions.
design: Do not model the carrier as an ordinary fee-paying EIP-1559 transaction whose 30,000 gas must cover calldata and execution. The 30,000 field is canonical visible accounting; authenticated OCOMP execution is routed before ordinary intrinsic-gas handling and is bounded by the system work schedule. The embedded OCOMP signature and pinned snapshot remain authorization authority.
acceptance_criteria: Every canonical OCOMP vote carrier has gas_limit exactly 30,000; malformed or unauthorized lookalikes fail closed. Valid votes bypass ordinary intrinsic-gas/fee debit, consume zero user-lane budget, and consume bounded system work. Proposer, import and historical replay produce identical receipts/state. Oversized work fails atomically. Old 9M/30M envelope assumptions and temporary markers are absent. Focused pool/executor/zero-fee/system-budget tests pass.
close_reason: Canonical 30k validator-authenticated OCOMP system carrier, pinned-snapshot authorization, zero user-lane accounting, bounded internal system work, txpool admission, supervisor submission, docs and focused tests are GREEN.

title: P9: one-hour OCOMP compute-vote window and deadline jail
description:
## Goal

Give every finalized OCOMP attempt one exact compute-and-vote window of 1800 blocks. Every member of the pinned ACTIVE snapshot must submit a valid included vote before the exclusive deadline, even when quorum applies the result earlier.

## Deadline transition

At the exact deadline a deterministic system transition compares the pinned participant set with timely valid vote slots. Every missing participant is sent immediately to JAILED with idempotent JobId/participant evidence. Timely present voters are not classified as missing. On-chain inclusion is the only provable vote.

## Workflow

Implement test-first and update existing ADRs/docs in the same slices.
design: On-chain inclusion is the only provable vote. Broadcasting without inclusion does not satisfy the obligation. Start the compute-vote window from the finalized job binding so forks do not create slashable phantom obligations.
acceptance_criteria: The finalized attempt stores an exact start height and exclusive deadline=start+1800. Votes before deadline are timely; votes at/after deadline are late. Quorum does not close remaining slots. Deadline handling jails each missing pinned validator exactly once, is replay-safe, handles all-voted/one-missing/multiple-missing/already-jailed-or-exited cases, and affects future ACTIVE snapshots through the existing validator lifecycle. Historical 4→5 jobs use their own pinned sets.
close_reason: Implemented and verified the exact 1800-block compute-vote window, continued voting after quorum, deterministic deadline accountability/jail, historical snapshot behavior, retention bounds, fixtures and reachable harness profiles; focused and package gates are GREEN.

title: P8: remove fixed live-job and OCOMP validator-count assumptions
description:
## Goal

Remove the arbitrary MAX_LIVE_JOBS=2 rule and every OCOMP-specific assumption tied to 256 validators. Each attempt is independently keyed by JobId and pins exactly the ordered ACTIVE ValidatorSet at its start. N and quorum come only from that snapshot.

## Constraints

Do not replace 2 or 256 with another OCOMP membership/count literal. Participant wire indices remain encoding fields, not product membership policy. Per-block processing and allocation remain deterministically bounded by existing protocol/system work limits; do not silently reintroduce a global live-job cap as backpressure.

## Workflow

Implement one observable RED→GREEN behavior at a time and update the existing ADRs/plan in the same slices.
design: Remove arbitrary global-count semantics, not resource accounting. Do not replace 2 or 256 with another unexplained literal. Keep wire participant indices as u16 encoding fields without presenting u16 as an OCOMP membership policy.
acceptance_criteria: No production constant, codec invariant, capacity assertion, fixture, ADR or guide treats two live jobs or 256 validators as an OCOMP product rule. Multiple live jobs remain independently addressable and cannot overwrite each other. Each job membership equals its pinned ACTIVE snapshot for every consensus-reachable N. Focused lifecycle/index/codec tests and final E2E pass.
close_reason: Removed OCOMP-specific live-job/member count assumptions; all RED/GREEN evidence, full regressions, generated shape, registry, reproducible final artifacts and documentation audit are green.

title: P11: FullNode independently executes and verifies Lysis fail-closed
description:
## Goal

Complete the current OCOMP epic with a mandatory FullNode follower. Every OCOMP-enabled FullNode consumes the finalized intent and authenticated source bodies/proofs, independently executes the same canonical Lysis program as validators, materializes the required local chunks/data, and compares digest, roots and manifest with the quorum result before accepting its activation.

## Role boundary

A FullNode never votes and needs no OCOMP signing key, relay signer or validator-only config. Ordinary canonical EVM replay is insufficient: missing bodies/proofs, local compute failure or any digest/root/manifest mismatch is fail-closed and observable.

## Workflow

Implement focused RED→GREEN slices through production interfaces, then prove the behavior in the reachable process E2E.
acceptance_criteria: A FullNode independently recomputes a reachable Lysis job, stores canonical local result data, accepts an exactly matching quorum result, rejects mismatch before activation, fails closed on unavailable authenticated inputs, and recovers correctly across restart. Validator and FullNode results/state agree in E2E while FullNode has no voting key or vote capability.
notes: This issue is no longer deferred outside the epic: the user explicitly included the FullNode follower in the active goal. It remains sequenced after dynamic membership/system-vote/deadline work.
close_reason: Implemented and verified mandatory keyless FullNode Lysis follower, durable exact-result authority, certified finality/retention wiring, restart verifier-chain recovery, q-forming fail-closed barrier, and current documentation.

title: P7: run dynamic OCOMP acceptance E2E and final regression gates
description:
## Goal

Final acceptance only after P8, P10, P9 and the FullNode Lysis follower are GREEN. Prove the reachable fresh-network workflow: node five first synchronizes as a true FullNode, later joins through registration/confirm-ready/DKG/ACTIVE, new jobs use the new ACTIVE snapshot, historical jobs retain their old snapshot, and all pinned members may continue voting after quorum until the 1800-block deadline. At deadline every missing pinned member is recorded in accountability; only a member whose current status is still ACTIVE is transitioned to JAILED, while non-ACTIVE statuses are not mutated and cannot make the deadline block fail. FullNodes independently reproduce and verify Lysis.

## Required evidence

Use the existing reachable 4→5 topology only as an E2E example, never as protocol architecture. Prove proposer/import/replay agreement for the canonical 30,000-gas system vote carrier; prove no vote or deadline work consumes the user 30M gas lane; prove restart/exact retry and independent FullNode fail-closed behavior. Run all quality gates and documentation consistency checks.

## Scope

This task adds no new product behavior except defects strictly required by its already-specified acceptance scenario. Basic behaviors must already have focused RED→GREEN evidence in their owning tasks.
design: One combined world must exercise OCOMP and the existing joiner/DKG machinery. Do not simulate membership by directly writing ACTIVE status or by using activate_validator.
acceptance_criteria: All prerequisite tasks are closed; reachable validator/joiner/historical-job/deadline-jail/FullNode scenarios pass; system votes and deadline work do not consume the user gas lane; proposer/import/replay and FullNode state/results agree; required ADRs/docs contain only the target dynamic model; workspace tests, fmt, Clippy, machete, registry/shape/capacity, fixture reproducibility and layout-hash gates pass.
notes:
Staged acceptance per user: before main integration finish source, documentation, and executable E2E definitions; run only formatting, compile/check, and E2E-harness compilation. Do not run process E2E before merging main. Prepare one coherent pre-main commit, then wait for explicit command. After merging HTTP/ZeroMQ supervisor/workers changes from main, adapt transport wiring and only then run full process E2E/final gates. The attempted @ocomp-dynamic-admission runtime was stopped on user correction; it did prove the narrow follower pre-start mailbox deadlock fix reached finalized height 24, but this is not final acceptance evidence.
FINAL ACCEPTANCE 2026-08-11: reachable dynamic OCOMP evidence is GREEN. Release real SGX/no-attest run passed 13/13: live DKG/reshare 4->5, old 4/q3 and new 5/q4 snapshots coexist, fifth validator votes, deadline accountability jails only missing current ACTIVE, keyless FullNode computes without voting, and restart preserves historical/current jobs. Late carrier status-0 behavior is covered by commit bb328729 and fresh 10/10 OCM-PUB-003. System carrier/quality/documentation gates are green. Evidence /tmp/outbe-e2e-dynamic-live-dkg.CIdrzV/evidence/scenario-001.json sha256 07996b47718cd81602ce17aa46447ea41fcee1bfbf25fee36d5c2f2e0e477147.

Real rerun command: cargo run --locked -p outbe-e2e-harness --features ocomp-integration --bin outbe-e2e -- --tee mock --validators 4 --all --tags '@ocomp-dynamic-overlap'. Exact code diagnosis: Supervisor signs every vote with MAX_ZERO_FEE_OCOMP_GAS_LIMIT=max_activation_gas=30,000,000; protocol steady block gas limit is 30,000,000; payload builder admits a pool tx only when cumulative begin gas + tx gas_limit + reserved end-system gas <= block gas limit. Mandatory system gas is nonzero, so a 30M vote cannot ever be selected. Existing consensus-bound capacity gate multiplies 30M by the response window but does not prove transaction schedulability. Per plan section 11 and blocker protocol, three independent agents are attacking the same gas-envelope fix before any production change.

comments.author: Aleksandr
comments.text: RED-27 three-agent cross-review converged (2026-08-05): a smaller evidence-backed supervisor vote envelope is necessary but insufficient for the plan's consensus-bound capacity claim. MAX_VALIDATORS=256 gives q=171; two concurrently live voting jobs require 342 votes over 64 blocks, therefore at least 6 schedulable votes per steady block. CycleTick currently may consume the full begin-system remainder, so the plan's guarantee requires a consensus-visible gas reserve that leaves room for 6 measured vote envelopes plus mandatory end-system gas. Existing txpool priority/defer is reusable; no new P2P lane or defer subsystem is needed. Required user decision before production edits: confirm retaining 30M steady block / 64-block window / 2 live jobs / MAX_VALIDATORS and adding the computed CycleTick reserve. RED gate must first prove max-shaped q-forming EVM gas with headroom < available per-vote budget; if it cannot, stop again for a choice among block gas, deadline, concurrency or q-apply architecture. Goal remains active; P7 implementation is paused only at this explicit design gate.

comments.text: THREE-AGENT VALIDATION BLOCKER at HEAD 127a0d23 after merging origin/main b4e93f6c. All three independent reviews and cross-review agree P7 is not acceptable. F1: node retention treats Completed or Conflicted as terminal at first quorum, removes the job from live discovery and signing, so a pinned validator offline before discovery cannot restart and submit its mandatory post-quorum vote before the 1800-block deadline. F2: deadline close reuses generic jail_validator; PENDING causes Revert promoted to Fatal, while EXITING, UNBONDING and INACTIVE do not become JAILED, violating total deterministic missing-vote punishment and potentially halting the exact deadline height. Required minimum before P7 continues: tests and fixes for post-quorum discovery/restart, total idempotent deadline sanction, deadline-1 stale carrier proposer/import parity, saturated mixed-block carrier, and old-key reentry policy; then rerun the combined dynamic E2E and final gates. comments.author: Aleksandr
comments.text: User decision (2026-08-06), correcting deadline sanction semantics: an attempt continues to use its frozen historical ACTIVE ValidatorSet snapshot for vote eligibility, quorum, slots and missing_bitmap. At the exclusive deadline, each missing pinned participant is handled according to its current ValidatorSet status. Only a participant that is still ACTIVE transitions ACTIVE -> JAILED. If it is already JAILED or currently PENDING, REGISTERED, EXITING, UNBONDING, INACTIVE or EXITED, deadline closure records it as missing in the immutable accountability summary but performs no validator-state mutation and must not return Revert/Fatal. The deadline transition remains replay-idempotent. Never recompute the attempt membership from current ValidatorSet.

comments.author: Aleksandr
comments.text: User decision on reviewed stale-carrier scenario (2026-08-06): do not expand P7 with a special late-vote/tombstone/grace-window protocol. OCOMP vote carriers already have priority over ordinary user transactions and the acceptance evidence must prove that priority in a saturated mixed block. Consensus timeliness is determined only by inclusion_height < exclusive_deadline; local mempool arrival time is neither shared nor provable, so a carrier included at or after deadline remains late even if one node saw it earlier. A hypothetical carrier lingering locally past deadline is not a product-design blocker for this goal and does not justify changing the deadline semantics.

comments.author: Aleksandr
comments.text: Correction superseding the immediately preceding stale-carrier decision: a recognizable, authentic OCOMP system vote carrier may still be included after its job's exclusive deadline. Execution must not count a vote and must not abort payload construction/import/replay. It returns a deterministic controlled DeadlinePassed revert, producing a normal failed transaction receipt (status 0); the block continues. Standard Ethereum receipts do not carry revert text, so the reason is exposed through execution/RPC trace or structured error, while the receipt records failure. The carrier remains in the bounded system-work path and does not consume user gas. This requires enough retained closed-job authorization/binding data to distinguish an authentic late OCOMP carrier from arbitrary fee-free calldata. Normal in-window carriers retain highest transaction priority.

title: P6: rebuild OCOMP genesis, keygen, registry, fixtures and capacity evidence
description:
## Mandatory test-first execution

Implement this task as vertical RED → GREEN cycles. Before each production change, add one focused behavioral test through a public/production interface, run it, and record the exact command plus the expected failure in the issue notes. Add only enough production code to make that test and its nearest regression pass, then continue with the next behavior. The Tests section below is a behavior backlog, not a post-implementation phase. Never refactor while RED.

## Goal

Make fresh-network preparation produce dynamic ValidatorSet OCOMP registrations and regenerate every canonical artifact after protocol/runtime changes, with no fixed four-member committee.

## Files owned by this task

- scripts/seed_genesis.py
- bin/outbe-keygen/src/main.rs and tests
- bin/outbe-chain/src/ocomp_genesis.rs and tee/genesis composition tests
- xtask/src/ocomp/finalize.rs, capacity.rs and registry command wiring
- crates/system/ocomp-protocol generated_registry.rs, generated_shape.rs, generated_limits and registry generated documentation as final regeneration outputs
- testing/e2e-harness/fixtures/ocomp-final-v1/artifacts/* and root protocol-bundle-v1.ocb1
- testing/e2e-harness/src/ocomp_evidence/* and metadosis_evidence verification that consumes generated artifacts
- canonical genesis JSON/config bytes and fixture manifests affected by OcompForkInstallV1

## Genesis bootstrap

1. outbe-keygen ocomp no longer asks for fork id, protocol bundle hash, validator index or height validity. It derives validator identity with the shared helper from validator address plus the current 48-byte BLS MinPk public key and emits the simplified canonical registration and secret key.
2. Genesis tooling accepts Vec registrations exactly matching the ordered genesis ValidatorSet, not a four-element array. It validates chain/genesis identity, validator identity, PoP, purpose, key epoch and unique keys.
3. Do not reintroduce a static OCOMP committee. Founder registrations are bootstrap key material only; voting membership always comes from ValidatorSet snapshots.
4. Avoid a genesis-hash fixed-point: writing a PoP that binds genesis_hash into genesis alloc would change the state root and therefore genesis_hash. Keep the canonical founding registration Vec in the chain-config fork-install artifact, which is outside the genesis header commitment, and import it atomically into ValidatorSet at OCOMP lifecycle activation after validating it against the already-seeded ACTIVE addresses and BLS keys. seed_genesis.py prepares/validates the matching validator records but must not mutate the post-hash alloc with genesis-bound PoP bytes.
5. OcompForkInstall canonical bytes contain protocol/profile authority and founder registrations, but no result committee, member indices, threshold or committee hash. Installation is exact-replay idempotent and fails if the registration set does not exactly cover genesis ACTIVE validators.

## Capacity and generated artifacts

1. Replace fixed arrays and POC_COMMITTEE_SIZE in genesis, finalize, evidence and fixtures with bounded Vec values and u16 indices.
2. Synthetic shape/capacity checks read the exported current consensus validator bound; OCOMP production code contains no membership-count literal and no private cap.
3. Measure codec/storage size of the monolithic accountability blob, one-vote gas/internal work, number of votes fitting in the response window, dynamic bitmap/evidence size and finalization decode at the consensus bound.
4. A failed gate is a blocker. Do not silently cap membership, change the ValidatorSet or introduce decomposed vote state without a new user decision.
5. Regenerate protocol registry, schema/preimage docs, shape constants, canonical install bytes, protocol bundle, network-binding/capacity evidence and fixture hashes deterministically.

## Documentation owned by this task

- Update docs/adr/blockchain/ADR-B-GEN-001-genesis-chain-identity-and-schema-activation.md and ADR-B-CAP-001-resource-metering-and-capacity-closure.md for founder key bootstrap, absence of genesis membership and the consensus-derived capacity bound.
- Update README.md, off-chain-computation.md and off-chain-poc.md to the implemented dynamic model. Remove obsolete fixed-membership claims; Git history is the history.
- Regenerate generated-registry.md, generated-shape-freeze.md and all canonical artifact documentation from the new forms.

## Tests and commands

- outbe-keygen registration roundtrip and wrong address/BLS/genesis rejection.
- genesis accepts arbitrary valid ValidatorSet length within consensus config, rejects missing/extra/reordered/duplicate registrations, and installs all registrations atomically.
- fixture generation is byte-reproducible from a clean checkout.
- cargo xtask ocomp registry --check.
- OCOMP shape/capacity checks at the exported consensus bound.
- explicit assertion that METADOSIS_STORAGE_LAYOUT_V1_HASH is unchanged and the reserved static-committee slot is zero.

## Out of scope

No production/testnet hardware evidence and no DCAP changes. No OCOMP key rotation.
design: Founder registration material may be static input because it bootstraps keys, not membership. The exact ordered ACTIVE ValidatorSet remains the only voting membership source after installation.
acceptance_criteria: Fresh genesis preparation has no static result committee, every genesis ACTIVE validator receives one validated stored OCOMP registration at lifecycle activation, all canonical artifacts regenerate reproducibly, registry and shape checks pass, and capacity passes at the current consensus bound or the issue stops as a reported blocker. For every implemented behavior, the issue contains RED command/failure evidence followed by focused GREEN evidence; production code was not written before its behavioral test. Every documentation path assigned to this task describes the same GREEN production behavior; the task cannot close with stale fixed OCOMP membership, quorum or slot assertions.
notes: Plan mapping: sections 6, 8 and 9 for fresh-genesis tooling, artifacts, registry/fixtures and consensus-bound shape/capacity evidence.
