title: Preserve daily emission conservation
description: Fix validator top-up rounding residue ownership, make allocation arithmetic fail closed, and remove the unused contradictory best-effort dispatcher. Fresh-genesis-only cutover. No emission percentages, cap formula, ABI, storage, wire, Gem policy, or Oracle liveness changes.
design:
SCOPE: Rewards top-up outcome, Cycle fresh-settlement residue routing, EmissionLimit pure allocation arithmetic, separate dead-dispatcher removal, tests and ADRs. Fresh-genesis-only. NON-GOALS: activation/migration, percentages/cap formula, eligibility/fees/Gem policy, Oracle liveness, ABI/events/wire/storage changes, corrupted-state recovery, and new Cycle halt conditions.

INVARIANTS: (1) For a fresh top-up settlement, distributed Gems + validator terminal excess == validator allocation; validator excess = validator allocation - distributed = fees + rounding residue. (2) AlreadySettled never remints and is never interpreted as fresh undelivered top-up; Cycle preserves prior liveness by contributing fees only. (3) Empty or zero-total participation creates no Gems and routes the full validator allocation to the terminal sink without halting. (4) All Cycle effects share one checkpoint; failure leaves no Gem, guard, receipt, or cursor write and retry is exact. (5) Valid bounded allocations remain exact and sum to total; arithmetic overflow returns a typed error. (6) Production delivery remains all-or-nothing; the unused best-effort dispatcher is removed separately.

TRANSITIONS: paired whole-day settled markers => no-op; existing marker/receipt mismatch => existing Fatal unchanged; zero allocation/no voters/fees>=allocation => full validator allocation terminal without top-up call; fresh Settled{distributed} => mint then validator_excess=validator_amount-distributed; fresh non-empty zero-total => Settled{0}, no Gem, full validator allocation terminal, continue; AlreadySettled with open whole day => no remint, validator_excess=fees, continue without new Fatal/Revert; mint/downstream failure => whole-trigger rollback then deterministic retry. Pure allocator: invalid table retains existing errors; bounded valid input returns exact allocations; mul/add/sub overflow returns stable typed errors.

CANONICAL TYPES: source-only TopupSettlementOutcome::{Settled{distributed: U256}, AlreadySettled}; no canonical wire/state/ABI type changes.

OWNERSHIP/PATHS: Rewards API owns the source-only outcome and participation math (crates/system/rewards/src/api.rs); Cycle owns reconciliation and terminal routing (crates/system/cycle/src/handler.rs plus tests/lib docs); EmissionLimit owns checked pure allocation (crates/system/emissionlimit/src/allocation.rs); a later mechanical PR removes dispatch_allocations and the sole direct tracing dependency; ADR-S-RWD-001 and ADR-S-EMI-001 own normative documentation. Current Rewards/Cycle WIP correction is the final allowed semantic correction pass.

PR ORDER: PR0 test-only Oracle freshness fixture (complete); PR1 top-up conservation without new halt conditions; PR2 checked allocator; PR3 mechanical dead dispatcher removal. TESTS: one Bead per RED/characterization; focused/full Rewards/Cycle/EmissionLimit nextest, clippy -D warnings, fmt check, diff check. No Gherkin/SGX E2E because no external/process/TEE seam.
acceptance_criteria: Focused Rewards, Cycle, and EmissionLimit tests pass; full package suites, clippy, fmt check, and diff check pass; no unplanned production paths; scope audits pass.
notes: Architecture matrix (explicit): WholeDayClosed + any event -> no-op; replay is exact; restart reads durable closed markers; deadline N/A. WholeDayOpen + zero allocation/no voters/fees>=allocation -> no top-up call, full validator allocation to terminal, settle; replay then follows WholeDayClosed; restart resumes from unchanged/open or durable closed state; deadline N/A. WholeDayOpen + fresh non-empty positive participation -> Rewards Settled{distributed}, mint floor shares, Cycle routes validator_amount-distributed to terminal, then closes; mint/downstream error rolls back every effect and exact retry repeats; restart sees only fully committed or fully rolled-back state; deadline N/A. WholeDayOpen + fresh non-empty zero-total -> Settled{0}, no Gem, full validator allocation terminal, continue; replay/restart as above; deadline N/A. WholeDayOpen + Rewards AlreadySettled -> no remint, fees only to terminal reconciliation, continue without new error; restart/replay preserve prior Gem/guard; deadline N/A. Marker/receipt mismatch -> existing Fatal before effects; replay/restart repeats same Fatal until repaired; deadline N/A. Pure allocator + valid bounded total -> exact allocations summing total; overflow -> typed Revert/no output; replay/restart deterministic; actor/deadline N/A. Actor is the critical Cycle daily dispatcher for settlement rows and a pure caller for allocator rows.
close_reason: Implemented as four stacked green slices. Full gate: 117/117 nextest PASS; clippy -D warnings PASS; fmt/diff PASS. Final independent Standards and Spec re-reviews found no blocker. No new Cycle halt, ABI/wire/storage, Oracle-liveness, or emission-policy change.

title: Close Oracle WWD, registries, reference S-curve, and consumer pricing gaps
description: Implement only the agreed requirements from Where Outbe Prices Come From: exact WorldwideDay VWAP, default six-currency reference registry, an independent policy-rate registry inside Oracle, a continuous S-curve chain per reference currency, S-curve use only in Tribute nominal pricing, and VWAP-only Nod and OCOMP entry pricing. Work is fresh-genesis-only and test-first in dense PR waves.
design:
ARCHITECTURE FREEZE

Fixed point: main at 9f5375aa.

Scope:
1. Exact WWD VWAP over the closed half-open interval [midnight UTC - 50,400 seconds, plus 50 hours).
2. Reference currencies default to the strictly ascending set [156,344,392,826,840,978].
3. Policy rates are an independent Oracle registry; default is only USD 840 at 36,300 in scale 1e6.
4. One continuous S-curve chain per reference currency.
5. S-curve affects only encrypted Tribute nominal pricing.
6. Nod and authenticated OCOMP entry pricing use WWD VWAP only.

Non-goals:
- no Oracle tally, feeder, voting, reward, slashing, quorum, or reference-pair redesign;
- no Credis economics or FSM work; only a mechanical Oracle policy getter rename;
- no new system contract or precompile;
- no OCOMP opening wire or slot compaction;
- no migration, V2, legacy adapter, or fallback path;
- no automatic pair registration from reference or policy registries.

Canonical state and compatibility:
- Fresh genesis only.
- Existing TributeData layout and public ITributeFactory ABI stay unchanged. TributeData.tribute_price_minor changes semantic to the effective reference price max(V_ref,S_ref).
- OracleGenesisConfig contains reference_currencies: Vec<u16> and policy_rates: Vec<PolicyRate>.
- PolicyRate contains iso_code: u16 and annual_rate_1e6: U256.
- Oracle ABI keeps getReferenceCurrencies, replaces getCurrencyRate(uint16) with getPolicyRate(uint16), and adds getPolicyRateCurrencies. Missing policy returns NoPolicyRate.
- Oracle slot 60 is retired and never read or reused.
- WWD partial aggregates own slots 70 through 73: suffix price-volume and volume for [10:00,24:00), prefix price-volume and volume for [00:00,12:00), keyed by pair and UTC-day timestamp.
- Policy currency list and policy map own slots 74 and 75.
- Existing S-curve slots 34 through 39 remain canonical.
- Existing OCOMP opening bytes and storage-slot proof grammar remain byte-identical; the evaluator ignores S-curve values.
- Existing Tribute encrypted offer is changed in place, not versioned: remove host-computed tribute_price_minor and carry issuance_wwd_vwap_minor, reference_wwd_vwap_minor, and reference_scurve_minor, all scale 1e6 for the same WWD.

Invariants and owners:
- Oracle runtime owns exact half-open VWAP arithmetic and atomic overflow behavior.
- Oracle state/schema own aggregate and registry persistence.
- Oracle genesis owns sorted, unique, bounded reference and policy validation; maximum six references; USD reference is mandatory; registries remain independent.
- Oracle scurve owns one allocated chain per pair, deterministic continuation, peak replacement, and overflow-safe arithmetic.
- Oracle lifecycle owns once-per-day processing and reference-only traversal after activation.
- TEE protocol/codec own authenticated canonical bytes; enclave compute exclusively owns Tribute nominal arithmetic.
- TributeFactory owns only fetching typed Oracle inputs, calling TEE, validating the returned result, and persisting the existing TributeData field.
- Lysis and Oracle openings own their independent VWAP-only entry-price reads.
- No downstream module may reconstruct or apply the S-curve outside Tribute pricing.

WWD transition matrix:
- Snapshot before 10:00 UTC updates daily and prefix only.
- Snapshot at 10:00 UTC updates daily, prefix when before 12:00, and suffix from 10:00 inclusive.
- Snapshot at 12:00 UTC updates daily and suffix; prefix excludes 12:00.
- Snapshot before 24:00 updates daily and suffix.
- WWD snapshot composes prior-day suffix plus full target UTC day plus following-day prefix.
- Empty pair is omitted; all pairs empty is a deterministic no-op.
- Invalid canonical bounds reject without writes.
- Missing required aggregate history rejects rather than approximating.
- Any checked arithmetic failure rolls back all writes.
- General explicit-range VWAP uses daily aggregates only for fully covered days and raw snapshots for edge fragments; exact bounds are never rounded.

Registry transition matrix:
- Fresh genesis validates strictly ascending unique references, length at most six, valid ISO codes, and mandatory USD.
- Policy entries validate unique valid ISO codes and positive bounded rates; policy presence does not require reference or pair presence and vice versa.
- Pair registration remains independently explicit.
- Absent policy getter returns NoPolicyRate.
- Import/export and seed materialization reproduce canonical bytes and slots.

S-curve transition matrix:
- No chain plus confirmed D-3 < D-2 > D-1 peak allocates one entry anchored at D-2.
- No confirmed peak is a no-op.
- Existing chain at candidate day computes current S. A strictly higher confirmed peak replaces peak day and anchor in the same entry; lower or equal peak is ignored.
- elapsed period = days/128 and offset = days%128. Anchor period zero is the peak; each successor anchor is floor(previous*920000/1000000); current S is floor(period_anchor*coefficient[offset]/1000000).
- Day 127 to 128 is continuous and never evicts the chain. Multi-period evaluation is deterministic and overflow-safe.
- Replay of an already processed day is a no-op under the watermark.
- Before the consumer cutover PR, the engine remains correct under existing pair traversal. The activation PR atomically switches lifecycle processing to registered reference currencies with registered priced pairs only.
- Market at or above S yields no economic brake; later market below S can re-engage the same mathematical chain.

Tribute and Nod transition matrix:
- TEE inputs are issuance WWD VWAP, reference WWD VWAP, and reference S-curve for one WWD.
- effective_ref=max(V_ref,S_ref).
- nominal=floor(A_iss*1,000,000*V_ref/(V_iss*effective_ref)) using widened intermediates and one final floor.
- Missing or zero required VWAP rejects. Positive input rounding to zero rejects. Overflow rejects atomically.
- Same-currency and cross-currency flows use the same formula.
- Host persists effective_ref into existing TributeData.tribute_price_minor.
- Lysis and OCOMP always use WWD VWAP, even when S is higher.
- TEE failure, mismatch, replay, and restart retain existing fail-closed transport and persistence behavior.

Delivery workflow:
- PR0 is this freeze and Beads graph only.
- PR1 exact WWD aggregation.
- PR2 independent registries.
- PR3 continuous S-curve engine while retaining existing traversal.
- PR4 atomic reference-only activation plus Tribute TEE and Nod/OCOMP consumer cutover plus E2E.
- Every slice is independently correct and green.
- Dense test-first waves: add every agreed RED test for a slice together, then one dense GREEN implementation pass, then polish and scope audit. A hot production file receives at most implementation plus one integration-correction semantic pass.
- Any new invariant, transition, canonical type, required production path outside the issue map, or third semantic hot-file pass triggers STOP, three independent read-only audits, Telegram consensus report, and explicit user approval before resuming.
- Harness-only corrections supported by evidence may proceed without user approval.
- Telegram status is sent at start, every 30 minutes, on slice completion, and on blockers.

E2E decision:
- Extend tribute.feature scenario One public Tribute has complete projection and duplicate protection with cross-currency effective-reference and nominal assertions because it already owns encrypted ingress and projection.
- Extend the first ocomp.feature scenario A public Tribute completes real OCOMP FullNode verification NOD replay and contributor payout with explicit proof that Lysis and OCOMP entry prices equal WWD VWAP even when S is higher.
- Add a separate controlled-time Oracle/S-curve scenario only if unit plus existing lifecycle tests cannot prove day-127/day-128 continuation through production begin-block without obscuring the Tribute/OCOMP flows. This is an evidence-structure decision, not permission to change product scope.
- Release system evidence runs outside sandbox with sudo, release profile, sgx-no-attest, real Gramine SGX, no DCAP or QVL, and chain id 54322345.
acceptance_criteria: All four PR children are closed with their targeted unit, integration, format, clippy, and scope-audit evidence. Exact WWD boundaries, independent registries, continuous reference S-curve, Tribute-only brake, and Nod/OCOMP VWAP-only behavior are proven. Existing E2E scenarios are extended where they already own the path; a new scenario exists only if the recorded evidence analysis proves it necessary. Final release SGX/no-attest evidence is clean. No non-goal production path is touched.

Final worktree adds scoped Oracle edge/freshness/Gem corrections and release feeder/settlement evidence. Gates: production 379/379, clippy/fmt/diff/Forge/MCP PASS, R11 and R13 release SGX clean.

title: Build finalized Radicle topology and repository reconciliation
description:
## What to build

Implement the dormant RadicleManager with exact finalized readers, accepted signed endpoint directory, native Heartwood UDS adapter, read-only outbe-radicle TCP status adapter, desired, resolved and unresolved topology planning, non-persistent session reconciliation, append-only repository Seed convergence, pure startup/runtime FSM, retry and backoff, and immutable status snapshots. Keep production wiring dormant.

## RED batch

Add the complete behavior suite for subscribe-before-sample; one-hash ValidatorSet and Registry reads; provider lag; finalized regression and conflict; active validator without NodeId; N=1, N=2, N=4 and N greater than the Heartwood default outbound limit; inbound-session satisfaction; lost-session repair; endpoint expiry and replacement; managed-only disconnect; external inbound preservation; full Seed Scope::All replay; desired, available and pending repository transitions through TCP status; partial UDS or TCP failure; manager restart; sidecar loss and recovery; pure Disabled, JoiningUnbound, Ready and RuntimeDegraded transitions; and shutdown.

## GREEN batch

Implement exact finalized reader, endpoint directory and refresh scheduler, planner, UDS and TCP adapters, manager FSM, progress tracking, and status handle.

## POLISH

Run manager integration tests with fake control/status adapters and real temporary UDS/TCP wire fixtures, affected exact-state readers, fmt, clippy, race and restart tests, and scope audit. Full outbe-radicle process startup/capacity is existing qrc.2 evidence; production process integration belongs to qrc.7 and release E2E to qrc.8.
design: The public module interface stays small: start, status snapshot, signed peers, and shutdown. ValidatorSet and Registry are read from one state_by_block_hash snapshot. UDS owns control; TCP status is read-only. qrc.6 owns the pure dormant FSM and accepted endpoint cache. qrc.7 alone owns production consensus gating and channel activation. Registry is append-only, so manager repeats Seed Scope::All for the full finalized set and has no Unseed path.
acceptance_criteria: ValidatorSet and Registry are read from the same exact finalized block hash without latest fallback. Desired, resolved, and unresolved peers and desired, available, and pending repositories are distinct and observable. Only managed outbound sessions are disconnected; external inbound sessions are preserved. Lost sessions and changed endpoints converge automatically. Every finalized RepoId is idempotently Seeded with Scope::All after startup and recovery, with no Unseed path. TCP status can change pending to available only when local Heartwood storage reports the repository readable; TCP status failure leaves availability unknown or pending, records failure, retries, and never gates consensus. last_seen_finalized and last_converged_finalized are distinct; convergence advances only after successful UDS policy and topology reconciliation, not on repository fetch completion. Runtime sidecar control loss degrades Radicle without stopping the abstract FSM. Simulated topology above the Heartwood default outbound limit proves the manager plans and requests the complete desired cardinality; qrc.2 wrapper evidence proves the derived Heartwood connection capacity. Dormant manager suites and real temporary UDS/TCP wire fixtures pass without production routing.
notes:
TCP status unavailability never gates consensus or changes desired policy. Repository availability remains unknown or pending, the failure is counted, and the manager retries within the frozen 5-second request deadline and its normal backoff.
qrc.6 freeze addendum approved after three-agent POLISH stop. Authoritative plan SHA256 cf502e635600498abc28157ca029db325d058019aee7857c68de8841b41cca99. Exact production paths: workspace Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock; crates/blockchain/radicle/Cargo.toml; src/lib.rs; src/manager/{mod,types,fsm,actor,adapters,snapshot}.rs. Exact tests: tests/{manager,manager_support,adapters}.rs plus snapshot.rs unit tests. Only manager/*.rs are qrc.6 hot production files; manifests/lib.rs are mechanical. qrc.5 endpoint paths and qrc.7 stack/channel/RPC/metrics paths are forbidden. Frozen integration-correction rows: pending and applied finality ordering/conflict; externally-tagged Heartwood session JSON; end-to-end DisconnectDisposition semantics; restart reconstruction of managed non-persistent outbound sessions under Network::Outbe+Static; phase_error preserves fatal FSM result and prevents convergence; exponential retry 1s..30s plus deterministic per-validator 0..250ms jitter, success reset, healthy repair default 30s. N>16 manager test proves cardinality; derived Heartwood capacity remains qrc.2 evidence.
Completion evidence: dormant RadicleManager implemented at plan SHA256 cf502e635600498abc28157ca029db325d058019aee7857c68de8841b41cca99. Exact finalized ValidatorSet+Registry snapshot, finalized fencing, signed endpoint cache, native Heartwood UDS control, loopback TCP repository status, managed outbound restart reconstruction, disposition-safe two-phase replacement, full Seed replay, fatal phase_error, exponential retry/jitter, status handle, shutdown. cargo test -p outbe-radicle: 43 passed; cargo test --release -p outbe-radicle: 43 passed; cargo clippy -p outbe-radicle --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo fmt --all --check and git diff --check passed. Three final independent audits PASS for standards/scope, outbe-chain spec and Heartwood compatibility. No qrc.5 endpoint path or qrc.7 production path touched.

title: Implement signed Radicle endpoint discovery over Commonware
description:
## What to build

Implement the canonical Radicle endpoint request, response, address codec, signature verifier, freshness rules, pending-request correlation, bounded unknown-anchor queue, and dormant Commonware actor/handle. Reserve channel 8 without activating production behavior. Keep the validator BLS private key inside its existing consensus-stack owner. Accepted topology cache and periodic repair belong to qrc.6.

## RED batch

Add complete golden and negative vectors for IPv4, IPv6 and DNS canonicalization; sort and dedup; bounded sizes; request nonce replay; chain and genesis separation; validator identity; on-chain NodeId match; BLS signature; immutable exact-anchor ValidatorSet input; TTL; unknown, future and stale anchors; inactive validators; malformed frames; request timeout; response correlation; and bounded pending queues.

## GREEN batch

Implement the codec, signer and verifier, pending-request table, bounded unknown-anchor handling, actor, and bounded handle. The verifier consumes an immutable exact-anchor ValidatorSet snapshot supplied by its caller and never opens latest state.

## POLISH

Run protocol and property tests, simulated Commonware peers, fmt, clippy, and dormant integration compile gates; perform scope audit before any stack wiring.
design: Channel 8 is registered only by qrc.7 before network.start. The signed body contains the request ID, version, chain ID, genesis hash, validator address, NodeId, canonical bounded addresses, exact anchor number and hash, and expiry under OUTBE_RADICLE_ENDPOINT_V1. qrc.5 owns request correlation and verifier output only. qrc.6 owns the accepted signed endpoint directory, refresh scheduler, and topology use.
acceptance_criteria: Wire encoding is canonical, bounded, domain-separated, and covered by golden vectors. Every accepted response is correlated to a pending nonce and verified against one immutable exact-anchor ValidatorSet snapshot. Invalid, replayed, wrong-chain, wrong-NodeId, inactive, malformed, oversized, stale, expired, unsolicited, or timed-out responses never reach manager reconciliation. BLS private material is neither duplicated nor exported. Actor and handle pass multi-peer simulation while remaining dormant; no provider reads, production channel registration, endpoint cache, or topology code enter this wave.
notes: Completed against authoritative plan SHA256 fbf625de1d3887be802db6f1c7b30af82b2a79802b6da7c13432f42ee74965dc. Implemented the dormant outbe-radicle endpoint module with canonical raw IPv4, raw IPv6 and UTS46 STD3 DNS addresses; exact ORAD request/response codec; canonical MinPk signing and exact-anchor verification; bounded pending and unknown-anchor state; send-failure cleanup; CSPRNG correlation; and a bounded actor/handle. Scope audit: expected and actual production paths match exactly: workspace Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock plus crates/blockchain/radicle Cargo.toml, src/lib.rs and src/endpoint/{mod,address,wire,authority,pending,actor}.rs. No stack, provider, channel registration, accepted directory, topology, RPC, metrics, Heartwood or deployment path changed. Every hot production file used the planned implementation pass plus one integration-correction pass; no third pass or new invariant occurred. Evidence: cargo test -p outbe-radicle PASS (25 tests); cargo test --release -q -p outbe-radicle PASS (25 tests); cargo clippy -p outbe-radicle --all-targets -- -D warnings PASS; cargo fmt --all --check PASS; git diff --check PASS. Tests cover golden bytes, maximum frame, address canonicalization, BLS domain/identity/chain/anchor/TTL failures, replay/correlation, send failure, timeouts, pending and unknown capacities, future exact-snapshot handling, actor mailbox/deadline/multi-peer exchange and property decode/roundtrips.
close_reason: Canonical signed endpoint protocol, bounded state machine and dormant actor are implemented and verified without scope drift.

title: Bind Radicle NodeId during validator registration
description:
## What to build

Add Heartwood-compatible Radicle key generation and atomically bind a unique Radicle NodeId during validator registration. Add ValidatorSet forward and reverse storage, registration signature V2, ABI and CLI updates, founder genesis materialization and validation, re-registration rules, cleanup, and registration-state tests. Production startup gating is not part of this wave.

## RED batch

Add all key-format fixtures; signature V2 golden and negative vectors; zero and duplicate NodeId; atomic rollback; forward and reverse consistency; founder genesis; inactive re-registration with the same or different NodeId; and final cleanup tests.

## GREEN batch

Implement keygen, ValidatorSet schema/runtime/precompile, Solidity and CLI callers, genesis seeding, registration helpers, and all caller updates in one coherent pass.

## POLISH

Run ValidatorSet, keygen, CLI, genesis, layout, fmt, clippy, and affected E2E compile gates. Audit that no endpoint state or production startup behavior entered this slice.
design: Use slots 59 and 60. There is no setRadicleNodeId operation. The fresh-network registerValidator contract uses the V2 selector and OUTBE_VALIDATOR_REGISTRATION_V2 domain. While an inactive record remains reserved, re-registration requires the same NodeId; a new NodeId is allowed only after final cleanup. qrc.6 owns the dormant JoiningUnbound FSM and qrc.7 owns production before-voting enforcement.
acceptance_criteria: outbe-keygen radicle emits native Heartwood-readable OpenSSH Ed25519 material with correct permissions and NodeId. Validator registration atomically stores unique non-zero forward and reverse NodeId bindings. Registration V2 binds version, chain ID, validator address, and NodeId under a new domain. Founders are fully seeded and validated in genesis. Re-registration and cleanup preserve forward and reverse consistency without stale reservations. title: Add the bounded permissionless Radicle repository registry
description:

title: Build the Outbe Heartwood profile and operator-managed sidecar
description:
## What to build

Add Network::Outbe with no public seeds, static peer behavior, explicit validator-scale connection limits, bounded idempotent disconnect, protected native UDS control, and read-only loopback TCP status for health and local repository availability. ## RED batch

## GREEN batch

Implement the Heartwood fork changes and wrapper until the whole batch passes. The wrapper loads an existing Heartwood key but never generates one. It starts native Heartwood Runtime with Outbe, Static, Relay::Always, Block seeding policy, configured limits and advertise addresses. UDS owns control; TCP status is read-only.

design: outbe-radicle is owned by the Heartwood-side slice and remains operator-managed. It reads no chain state, owns no EVM or BLS key, sends no transaction, and is never spawned by outbe-chain. Native UDS owns nid, config, sessions, connect, disconnect and Seed. Read-only loopback TCP exposes only health and local repository availability. Key generation belongs exclusively to qrc.3; qrc.2 uses a native fixture.

Required wrapper flags reject missing home, control socket, listen, advertise, max validators, external inbound reserve, or status listen. outbe-radicle starts native Heartwood Runtime with Static peers, Relay::Always, Block default seeding, configured advertise addresses, and connection limits sufficient for max validators plus the explicit inbound reserve. Native UDS uses a protected local path. disconnect_bounded terminates for connected, absent, pending, inbound, and changed-address cases. Read-only HTTP status binds loopback only, accepts no control commands, implements GET /healthz and the frozen versioned repository-availability route, enforces exact RepoId encoding, connection and deadline bounds, and distinguishes locally readable repositories from absent repositories. The wrapper never generates keys or owns its process lifecycle. Both repository slices are independently green and the consumed Heartwood revision is pinned.

## Objective

Implement the reviewed Radicle integration defined by /home/ubuntu/plan_radicle.md. Every Outbe validator runs an operator-managed outbe-radicle sidecar. Heartwood remains the Git, issues, patches, gossip, Noise, fetch, and storage data plane. outbe-chain owns validator NodeId binding, finalized repository policy, signed endpoint discovery over Commonware, native UDS reconciliation, read-only TCP availability observation, startup readiness, RPC, and metrics.

title: Implement hourly ProtocolCycle orchestration
description: Replace the separate daily emission and noon WWD triggers with one UTC-hour-aligned ProtocolCycle on a fresh chain. Cycle is the sole UTC-day orchestrator and invokes the existing EmissionLimit, Rewards, WorldwideDay, and Metadosis commands without changing their business internals. Missed UTC days during a multi-day chain halt are intentionally forfeited: they are not settled, materialized, rewarded, or replayed.
design:
ARCHITECTURE FREEZE (revised 2026-08-20)

Scope: fresh chain from block 0; ProtocolCycle replaces trigger id 0 and leaves id 2 reserved/inactive; production cadence is 3600 seconds aligned at HH:00 UTC; Cycle owns active_utc_day; existing EmissionLimit, Rewards, WorldwideDay, Metadosis, OCOMP, and Lysis business logic remains unchanged. Non-goals: no state migration, activation-height routing, legacy handler, governance update, synthetic missed-day WWDs, missed-day rewards, or unbounded catch-up.

Invariants: (1) Cycle slot 2 stores active_utc_day as YYYYMMDD and is seeded from root genesis timestamp. (2) Same UTC day performs no daily emission. (3) If block_day is the immediate calendar successor of active_utc_day, ProtocolCycle settles exactly active_utc_day through the existing daily emission command, advances the cursor to block_day only after successful settlement, and then invokes the existing composite WWD/READY flow once. (4) If block_day is more than one calendar day ahead, every completed day in the gap is forfeited: no EmissionLimit, Rewards settlement, receipt, WWD creation, Metadosis limit, Promis credit, or OCOMP work is synthesized; Cycle advances the cursor directly to block_day and invokes the existing composite WWD/READY flow once. (5) A future/invalid cursor is fatal. (6) Any command error propagates and outer CycleTick rollback preserves cursor, state, CE work, receipt, and event replay. (7) Existing Metadosis/OCOMP/Lysis terminal failure semantics remain unchanged. (8) Trigger backlog coalesces to one latest hourly execution/event. (9) Exact EVM authority grants one daily allocation binding only for the immediate-successor transition, never for skipped days, plus the existing one composite process binding. (10) ID 2 is permanently reserved and absent from the active registry.

Transition matrix: uninitialized at block 1 -> initialize existing genesis state and active_utc_day, no handler event; same-day hourly slot -> no emission, run composite WWD/READY once, consume slot on success; immediate next day -> settle old day, cursor=block_day, run composite once, consume slot; multi-day gap -> skip all missed days, cursor=block_day, run composite once, consume slot; cursor in future/invalid date -> fatal, no effects; emission failure -> fatal outer rollback and replay; composite WWD/READY failure -> fatal outer rollback and replay; later CycleTick trigger failure -> whole system transaction rollback and replay; same-parent replay -> identical state/CE roots, receipts, events, and gas; restart/reorg -> canonical Cycle cursor determines replay; phase deadline -> transition on first successful hourly ProtocolCycle at or after deadline.

Canonical state/wire types: Cycle storage layout remains marker slot 0, last_executed_at slot 1, active_utc_day slot 2; no public Solidity ABI or event wire-shape change; TriggerId::ProtocolCycle=0; numeric id 2 remains reserved. Internal day-action is a closed enum SameDay | SettlePrevious{day} | SkipMissed{from,to}; it is not persisted or exposed.

Ownership: Cycle owns calendar comparison, skip/settle decision, cursor, ordering, and trigger event. EmissionLimit/Rewards own daily calculation and settlement invariants. WorldwideDay/Metadosis own phase transitions, READY selection, failure terminalization, and Promis behavior. EVM precompile authority owns exact command entitlements and must derive the same day action.

Production paths/hot files: crates/system/cycle/{handler,runtime,triggers,schema,lifecycle}.rs; crates/blockchain/evm/{precompiles,executor,storage/ctx_provider}.rs; crates/blockchain/constants/src/lib.rs; crates/core/metadosis/{constants,runtime}.rs only for cadence-derived bounds/call seam; scripts/seed_genesis.py; focused Cycle/EVM/genesis tests; Cycle/EVM/Metadosis ADRs and protocol-constant docs. Historical reports are untouched.

Delivery: one independently green PR because registry, orchestration, exact authority, cadence, genesis seed, tests, and docs form one consensus seam. Tests first for same-day, contiguous midnight, multi-day forfeiture, invalid cursor, rollback/replay, authority, registry, cadence, genesis seed, and LocalNet behavior. Separate production release build without test features and accelerated release LocalNet build with test-protocol-overrides.
acceptance_criteria: Fresh block-1 initialization seeds active_utc_day without executing ProtocolCycle. Same-day hourly executions never form a daily limit. A contiguous next-day transition settles exactly one prior day before WWD/READY processing. A halt from day 17 to day 20 settles none of days 17-19, creates no missed-day receipts/WWDs/rewards, advances the cursor to day 20, and runs the existing composite WWD/READY flow once. Future/invalid cursors and command failures roll back the whole CycleTick and replay deterministically. Exact authority contains no missed-day allocation bindings. Trigger id 2 is inactive/reserved. Existing Metadosis/OCOMP/Lysis failure regression tests pass unchanged. Focused Cycle, EVM, constants, genesis, release builds, and accelerated SGX-no-attest LocalNet acceptance pass; the production release contains no test/E2E features.

Implementation and mock-LocalNet verification completed 2026-08-20. Tests: outbe-cycle 48/48; outbe-evm 198/198; seed genesis 9/9; constants default+test overrides pass; E2E harness all test targets compile and hourly helper tests pass; fmt and git diff check pass. title: Add height-gated hourly Metadosis Cycle flow
description:
Scope:
- Add a new stable Cycle trigger ID for an hourly Metadosis orchestrator.
- Preserve legacy EmissionLimit1 and WwdAdvanceNoon behavior before a compile-time activation height.
- After activation, retain legacy schedules/checkpoints/events but make their domain handlers no-op; enable the new hourly flow.
- The hourly flow optionally settles the previous UTC emission day, then always creates the current WWD, advances all active WWDs, and starts at most one new READY Metadosis/OCOMP candidate.
- Deliver the flow dormant until the operator supplies activation height X.

Explicit non-goals:
- Do not choose X in this slice.
- No Update/voting mechanism, genesis edit, storage migration, wipe, enclave/OCOMP change, protocol timing change, or processing of more than one new READY candidate.
- Do not alter EmissionLimitDaily arithmetic, WWD reducer rules, OCOMP request semantics, or other Cycle triggers.
design:
Architecture freeze

Invariants:
1. For every block before X, the new binary executes the legacy trigger set byte-equivalently: the new trigger is not anchored, emits no event, and writes no state.
2. Trigger IDs 0..4 never change meaning or numeric value; the new ID appends as 5. Cycle storage layout and all wire/state types remain unchanged.
3. Activation is determined only by consensus block height and a compile-time constant; never CLI/env/local config.
4. After X, legacy emission/noon handlers have no Metadosis/Rewards domain effects. Their existing checkpoints/events may continue.
5. The hourly handler treats (daily_settled, day_limit_receipt) as an integrity pair: (false,None) performs settlement; (true,Some) skips only settlement and continues lifecycle; mismatches are fatal.
6. A performed daily settlement preserves existing arithmetic, writes WorldwideDay[prev_day].metadosis_limit_amount plus its immutable receipt, and marks daily_settled only after the hourly lifecycle succeeds.
7. Every successful hourly execution creates current WWD if absent, exhaustively advances all due active-WWD phase edges, then starts at most one new READY candidate using its persisted metadosis_limit_amount.
8. The existing Cycle checkpoint makes the full handler atomic. Failure rolls back domain writes, trigger checkpoint, event, and CE work; the same slot retries on the next block.
9. Existing CycleTick Metadosis mutation bindings remain the sole authority: allocation, process-ready, and advance-due identities; no broader authority is introduced.

Transition matrix:
- Legacy mode, legacy emission due: existing daily settlement + start flow; existing success/error/replay behavior.
- Legacy mode, legacy noon due: existing active-WWD advance; existing success/error/replay behavior.
- Legacy mode, new hourly ID: not dispatchable; no checkpoint/event/state.
- First block at/after X, new hourly ID unseen: anchor its existing Cycle mapping entry to block timestamp; no handler; first deadline is the next UTC-hour slot.
- Activated mode, legacy emission/noon due: handler returns success without domain effects; dispatcher advances only that legacy checkpoint and emits its existing Cycle event.
- Activated mode, hourly due, pair absent: settle previous day, run WWD lifecycle, mark settled, checkpoint/event.
- Activated mode, hourly due, pair present: skip settlement only, run WWD lifecycle, checkpoint/event.
- Activated mode, hourly due, pair mismatched: fatal; full rollback; retry next block.
- Activated mode, hourly due, no READY WWD: successful no-op after creation/advancement.
- Activated mode, hourly due, READY WWD: start at most one new candidate; existing in-flight FSMs are preserved.
- Any handler/storage/CE error: full checkpoint rollback and next-block retry.
- Restart: read persisted trigger checkpoints; no replay of completed slot; pending due slot executes normally.
- Clock gap crossing multiple hourly deadlines: preserve dispatcher behavior of one scheduled slot per block until caught up.

Canonical shapes and compatibility:
- Append TriggerId::MetadosisHourly = 5.
- Add only internal mode/activation configuration types; no ABI, storage record, event, genesis, OCB1, or RPC shape changes.
- Reuse Cycle.last_executed_at and last_executed_block_number mappings and existing CycleTriggerExecuted event.

Ownership:
- outbe-cycle::triggers owns stable IDs, schedules, activation mode, and handler selection.
- outbe-cycle::runtime owns dispatch eligibility, anchoring, checkpoints, and retry.
- outbe-cycle::handler owns orchestration and daily-settlement skip/continue semantics.
- outbe-metadosis remains sole owner of WWD state/reducer, day-limit receipt, and READY processing.
- outbe-rewards remains sole owner of daily_settled.

Expected production paths / hot-file passes:
- crates/system/cycle/src/triggers.rs: one semantic implementation pass.
- crates/system/cycle/src/runtime.rs: one semantic implementation pass.
- crates/system/cycle/src/handler.rs: one semantic implementation pass.
- crates/system/cycle/src/lib.rs: documentation-only correction if required.
- Tests in crates/system/cycle/src/tests.rs and tests/model.rs; executor tests only if integration evidence requires them.

Ordered delivery slices:
1. This slice: dormant activation seam, new hourly flow, focused behavioral tests, scope audit; activation height remains disabled.
2. Later operator slice: set Some(X), rebuild release binary, run activation boundary/localnet evidence, deploy before X. No semantic redesign is permitted in slice 2.
acceptance_criteria:
- Focused tests prove no new ID state/event before activation.
- Tests prove first encounter at activation anchors and first fire is next UTC hour.
- Tests prove settled previous day skips only settlement while WWD lifecycle still runs.
- Tests prove an unsettled day is settled exactly once and marks daily_settled after successful lifecycle.
- Tests prove legacy handlers have no domain effects after activation and preserve old behavior before it.
- Tests prove mismatch/error rollback and restart/checkpoint behavior.
- Existing Cycle and Metadosis test suites pass.
- Cargo fmt, clippy for affected crates, and release outbe-chain build pass without test-protocol-overrides.
- Scope audit shows no state layout/genesis/enclave/OCOMP changes.
notes: Production activation re-freeze 2026-08-18: operator supplied current testnet height 170115 and requested activation in approximately 30 minutes. Public RPC measurement across heights 169242..170142 observed 900 blocks in 1914 seconds (2.127 s/block), so X is fixed at 170962 (=170115+847). Trigger ID 5 production schedule is unconditionally period=3600/offset=0, aligned to every UTC hour; metadosis.advanceIntervalSeconds must no longer affect ID 5 and remains owned only by the legacy dedicated WWD advancement trigger. At X the new trigger anchors without execution; first domain execution occurs on the first canonical block at or after the next whole-hour slot. No state/genesis/type changes. Required evidence: default and override trigger tables both show ID 5 period=3600/offset=0; boundary tests pass; release build passes. The earlier X=70/300-second evidence remains test-only historical evidence and is superseded for the production constant/schedule.

title: Make the embedded OCOMP Supervisor endpoint explicitly configurable
description: The node currently derives the embedded OCOMP Supervisor endpoint implicitly as loopback:(consensus listen port + 1). This hidden coupling makes port changes non-obvious, can create collisions, and requires Worker and SnapshotExporter environment files to duplicate an undocumented derivation. Add an explicit node CLI option such as --ocomp.supervisor-address, wire it into OcompExExConfigV1, expose it in deployment launchers, and make endpoint selection visible in startup logs. Preserve a documented compatibility policy for existing invocations.
design: Freeze the implementation model before production edits. Invariants: the endpoint must be loopback-only with a nonzero port; it remains node-owned and local-only; changing it must not affect genesis, chain identity, OCOMP boot nonce, protocol bundle hash, consensus state, or wire formats. Decide and document whether absence preserves the existing consensus-port-plus-one default or becomes a startup error. Ownership should remain in node CLI/config resolution, with the resolved address passed once into the embedded OCOMP runtime. Non-goals: changing Worker transport, introducing a standalone Supervisor process, or changing OCOMP protocol semantics.
acceptance_criteria: run.sh can set the Supervisor endpoint explicitly; the node honors and logs the resolved endpoint; non-loopback and port-zero values fail before services start; Worker and SnapshotExporter examples use the same explicit address; tests cover explicit configuration, the approved compatibility behavior when omitted, invalid endpoints, and removal of hidden overflow/collision ambiguity; release build and applicable OCOMP integration tests pass.

title: Design fresh-wipe OCOMP input export without duplicate Mongo projection
description: Investigate and freeze a replacement for RpcFinalizedProjectionV1 that keeps the node as the sole Mongo projection writer and removes the separate OCOMP projection database. The target network is always created after a complete wipe. Migration, backward compatibility, preservation of old projection state, genesis changes, and implementation in this task are explicit non-goals. Produce three independent interface designs, select one, define invariants and transitions from sealed WWD through certified retirement, map owning modules and hot files, explain the E2E coverage gap, and order test-first PR slices.
notes:
Three independent reviews completed. Selected design: separate SnapshotExporter reads the validator node's sole Mongo projection with read-only credentials; public RPC remains only for finalized authority, job discovery, and exact Lysis openings. Delete the _ocomp DB, RpcFinalizedProjectionV1, eth_getBlockReceipts replay, exporter writer lease, and retained Tribute body namespaces. Fresh-wipe cutover only: no migration, aliases, dual read/write, old schema support, or genesis changes. New materialization is allowed only while VotingOpen; Completed may reuse an already committed local CAS/receipt but may not reconstruct missing retired inputs. Full architecture freeze, transition matrix, ownership, tests, and PR slices delivered in session.
Architecture correction: removing retained inputs and forbidding first local computation after Completed breaks the existing FullNode trustless replay/readiness invariant. Current ocomp_exex explicitly starts FullNode compute on Completed; local compute failure is fatal and progress remains gated until local result is compared with canonical result. Fresh wipe does not solve late join/offline catch-up. Re-plan around a single node-owned Mongo projection plus minimal job-scoped move-on-retirement/verification hold; still remove the duplicate exporter projection and eth_getBlockReceipts replay.
Deferred by operator decision. Testnet and LocalNet retain the current separate per-validator _ocomp projection database for safety while the FullNode replay/retention architecture receives a dedicated multi-day analysis later.

title: Define mandatory response to revealed DKG shares for lagging ACTIVE validators
description: A release SGX/no-attest capacity run proved that an ACTIVE validator can fall behind execution before a reshare boundary, miss the 30-second DKG acknowledgement grace, and have its epoch threshold share deliberately disclosed in canonical dealer logs. In the observed run validator-2 was at execution height 242 while the other validators started reshare at height 270; its blocking Tribute enclave calls took about 10.8-11.5 seconds per two-Tribute block, it started DKG about 56 seconds late, and all four nodes reconstructed the same revealed validator. The current DKG fallback preserves liveness and BFT aggregate safety but makes the affected VRF partial publicly reproducible until key rotation. This issue must define and validate the mandatory protocol/operator response without changing NOD Materialization.
design: Treat DKG output.revealed() as a genuine security-degradation state, not a log exception. Analyze whether activation must stop, the validator must be automatically jailed or excluded from proposer selection, consensus-key rotation must be mandatory/automatic, or another bounded response is required. Cover repeated and multiple reveals, restart/replay, operator recovery, supported deployment topology, and whether co-located SGX execution starvation is a supported profile. Keep any consensus, ValidatorSet, DKG, and SGX-resource changes outside the NOD Materialization branch.
acceptance_criteria: The threat model quantifies what one and multiple revealed shares permit; the state transition and owner for detection, containment, key rotation, and recovery are frozen; production behavior and operational runbooks are covered by tests; normal production topology no longer leaves a revealed ACTIVE share in service without a deterministic response; the dedicated DKG reveal scenario remains fail-closed and ordinary E2E never allowlists an unexpected reveal.

title: Replace E2E free-text log exceptions with typed runtime audit events
description: The E2E strict runtime-log audit currently reconstructs request lifecycle state from English messages, Debug output, filenames, ANSI formatting, and line adjacency. This causes repeated harness rewrites when logging changes. Introduce one deep RuntimeLogAudit module and stable versioned tracing fields for the cancelled speculative payload deadline case, without changing consensus, payload execution, retry, timeout, or protocol behavior. Functional 257-NOD acceptance remains RPC/state/receipt based; runtime log hygiene remains a separate go/no-go gate.
design: Scope: typed audit normalization and policy for proposer cancellation plus body-read deadline; extract audit ownership from probes.rs; preserve legacy Update, DKG, and newPayload adapters without expanding them. Non-goals: global JSON logging migration, dedicated production audit journal, migration of all legacy text probes, consensus/control-flow changes, timeout/retry changes. Invariants: human message text, Debug formatting, ANSI, timestamps, line order, rotated filenames, and a prior process instance never authorize the new exception; only stable versioned event fields do. A deadline is accepted only when the same node source, process_instance, and payload_id has an explicit cancellation event. Missing/malformed/unknown/live-payload/conflicting typed events fail closed. Functional E2E never derives protocol success from logs. Canonical event shapes: proposal_view_cancelled_v1{audit_schema=1,process_instance,payload_id}; payload_execution_failed_v1{audit_schema=1,process_instance,payload_id,tx_hash,failure_kind}; process_instance is one node-process boot identity emitted identically by both producers; failure_kind is body_read_request_deadline or other_payload_execution_failure. Ownership: outbe-primitives runtime_audit_v1 owns schema constants and process identity; consensus handler emits cancellation identity; payload builder classifies and emits execution failure; RuntimeLogAudit owns discovery, normalization, policy, evidence; LocalNet launcher owns ANSI-free stdout. Transition matrix: (1) no cancellation + deadline failure for process P payload A => finding; (2) cancellation P/A + deadline failure P/A from same node source => one accepted cancellation episode; (3) cancellation P/A + failure P/B => finding; (4) cancellation P/A + failure Q/A => finding; (5) cancellation P/A + non-deadline failure P/A => finding; (6) cancellation without failure => informational; (7) exact duplicate cancellation/failure records => one episode; (8) conflicting failure kinds for one identity => finding independent of line/file order; (9) reordered/current/rotated records from same process => same outcome; (10) missing field, invalid process/payload/tx hash, unknown schema/event => malformed finding; (11) human message/Debug/ANSI/timestamp changes with canonical fields unchanged => no policy change; record severity is parsed only from the log header; (12) restart/replay => different process_instance prevents old records authorizing new failures; (13) pre-allocation cancellation without payload_id => ordinary debug information and cannot authorize any exception; (14) legacy newPayload/update/DKG events => existing exact adapters unchanged. Error behavior: audit parsing never affects node execution; malformed/unknown/conflicting audit events fail E2E evidence only. Deadline behavior: no protocol deadline changes; only classification after scenario. Expected production paths/hot files: primitives runtime_audit_v1 module plus lib export, handler.rs and payload_builder.rs, each one semantic observability pass plus one review correction pass. Harness paths: localnet/mod.rs one launch/integration pass, probes.rs one extraction pass, log_audit.rs implementation plus review correction pass, OCOMP timeout one pass. Tests/evidence: structural node classification; consensus payload trace; typed transition matrix including cross-process and conflicting duplicates; full harness suite; 257 SGX/no-attest evidence. Ordered delivery: one independently green PR slice on this branch: schema/process constants + producer fields + deep harness module + 600s test timeout; no production routing is incomplete because audit fields are observational and the harness consumes them in the same slice. Integration-correction pass is now used for the three review findings; a third semantic pass requires another stop. No second seam or future PR is required for correctness; legacy adapter migration is a separate future issue if requested.
acceptance_criteria: Focused audit tests pass; consensus trace test passes; no text/adjacency parser is added for proposer deadline; 257 Tribute -> Metadosis -> Lysis -> 257 NOD SGX/no-attest E2E is rerun with a 600-second materialization poll; diff contains no protocol or control-flow changes.
notes: Focused typed runtime-audit tests, consensus payload trace, payload failure classification, scoped Clippy, formatting, and harness compilation are green. The 257-NOD release SGX/no-attest run completed all 13 functional steps: 257 Tribute/NOD, real Metadosis/Workers/quorum/Lysis, bounded materialization, ordinary owner enumeration/nodData, restart persistence, and canonical reconstruction. The independent After-hook correctly rejected an unexpected canonical DKG share reveal caused by validator-2 execution starvation; that security issue is tracked separately as outbe-chain-5f5 and is not allowlisted or addressed by this audit change.
close_reason: Implemented stable typed payload-cancellation audit events and deep fail-closed runtime log correlation; focused release tests and scoped Clippy are green, and the 257-NOD production-path rerun completed all functional steps while correctly surfacing an unrelated canonical DKG security alarm tracked as outbe-chain-5f5.

description: Observation on clean HEAD 53d110dc during full SGX/no-DCAP E2E: validator-3 first rejected canonical block 327 because emission_limit_1/CycleTick hit BodyReadUnavailable: execution read request deadline exceeded, then immediately re-executed the same block/hash successfully and finalized it. comments.author: Aleksandr
comments.text:
ID: OCM26-BATCH3-CONSENSUS-LIVENESS-001.
Status: confirmed product liveness defect exposed by a test-profile regression; no code fix applied pending user decision.
Observed on clean daddba55: B12 batch=3 run /tmp/ocm26-470571-1786353361698/run-01 submitted three Tribute tx quickly, but receipt for the prior trio took 45.348s and the next trio timed out after 122.538s at head/finalized 54.
Expected: the capacity lane must advance 257 offers through valid blocks without receipt starvation; speculative work must not prevent canonical payload validation from meeting the consensus view budget.
Three independent read-only analyses agree on the causal chain: a 10-tx/10.27Mgas candidate containing three Tribute offers was admitted; Reth prewarm executed the three enclave-backed precompiles and canonical validation executed them again; all six process-local enclave requests serialized through the global RuntimeEnclaveClient Mutex. On validators 0/1 this took 31.9-32.0s, so only 2/4 validators voted before the view deadline (quorum 3/4). The view was nullified, a replacement block without the offers finalized, and the offers finalized on a later view/block. Thus 45s is failed view plus replacement/retry, not one slow finalization.
Excluded: RPC submission (58-76ms), txpool rejection, OOG, block gas exhaustion (10.27M/30M), system carrier failure, and permanent chain halt. Safety held; liveness/inclusion degraded severely.
Trigger versus root cause: changing the harness from the previously frozen concurrency 2 to 3 in daddba55 triggered the threshold, but the product defect is duplicate speculative plus canonical blocking enclave work and missing worst-case execution admission. Existing P0 outbe-chain-08n.6 owns the production correction. Disabling prewarm alone is not yet proven sufficient because three canonical approximately 5s SGX calls remain near the 15s effective timing budget.
Decision required before edits: (A) revert this evidence-only lane to batch=2 and finish B12 while retaining 08n.6 as a testnet P0, or (B) stop acceptance and architecture-freeze the consensus-sensitive production fix. Do not hide the issue by increasing receipt or consensus timeouts.

description:

title: Decouple genesis OCOMP activation from generic Update
description:
## Problem

A fresh wiped network already carries the immutable `OcompForkInstallV1` in genesis and executes `OcompLifecycleBegin` at block 1, but OCOMP readiness is still coupled to a synthetic generic Update proposal for protocol version 1. That Update contributes only two mutations: enabling the Tribute and Oracle OCOMP profiles. Tests then incorrectly use `active protocol version == 1` as proof that OCOMP activated.

## Goal

Make genesis-bound OCOMP operational immediately at its deterministic activation block (`H = 1` for a fresh network), without scheduling or activating a generic Update. Keep the generic Update subsystem unchanged for real future protocol upgrades.

## Scope

- Extend the existing atomic `install_fork_profile` command so the block-H `OcompLifecycleBegin` installs the Metadosis request profile/bundle, founder OCOMP registrations, Tribute OCOMP profile, and Oracle OCOMP profile together.
- Remove the OCOMP-specific protocol-v1 `UpgradeHandler`; retain an empty node-owned handler registry and the generic Update lifecycle.
- Stop injecting a synthetic scheduled Update into OCOMP genesis fixtures.
- Replace Update-version assertions in OCOMP integration/restart/mismatch tests with OCOMP-native state and behavioral evidence.
- Rewrite the existing OCOMP ADR and flow documentation to describe the actual single activation route.

## Explicit non-goals

- Do not remove or redesign generic Update/governance.
- Do not change `OcompForkInstallV1`, consensus wire formats, storage layouts, genesis hash construction, or founder registration format.
- Do not hardcode Tribute/Oracle storage slots in `seed_genesis.py`.
- Do not remove `activation_height`, Measurement/Final classifications, or legacy Final-profile support.
- Do not design in-place migration for an already-running network; rollout is by wipe.
- Do not refactor unrelated OCOMP lifecycle, networking, workers, retries, or retention.
design:
## Frozen implementation model

### Invariants

1. `OcompForkInstallV1` in the selected chain manifest is the sole genesis-bound OCOMP activation authority.
2. Before `H`, no Metadosis fork authority or owner OCOMP admission profile is active.
3. At exactly `H`, the receipt-visible `OcompLifecycleBegin` performs one checkpointed activation containing all four effects: founder registrations, Metadosis request profile/bundle, Tribute profile, and Oracle profile.
4. No OCOMP-specific `ScheduledUpdateInfo` is written and generic Update active version remains baseline (`0`) unless an independent real Update activates.
5. Exact pre-existing state is idempotent. Partial or conflicting state is fatal and is never repaired implicitly.
6. Any validation or storage failure rolls back every effect in all four owner modules; the activation block fails closed with no partial OCOMP readiness.
7. Later phases of block `H`, including the terminal OCOMP request route, observe the installed profiles. No governance transaction, extra block, or restart is required.
8. Replay and restart through `H` produce the same state. A manifest with a different immutable install remains fail-closed at `H`.
9. Generic Update activation, startup compatibility checks, and future upgrade handlers remain semantically unchanged.
10. Python genesis tooling never writes Rust-owned OCOMP profile storage slots directly.

### Transition matrix

| State | Event | Result | Error/replay/restart semantics |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fresh chain, height `< H` | normal block | OCOMP authority and all owner profiles remain absent | generic Update remains baseline |
| Fresh chain at `H`, valid install and owner prerequisites | `OcompLifecycleBegin` | all four effects commit atomically; same-block OCOMP lifecycle/request may proceed | success is deterministic |
| Height `H`, Oracle pair missing, Tribute state non-fresh, founder invalid, or install invalid | `OcompLifecycleBegin` | no effect commits | fatal system-tx failure; block rejected; wipe/genesis must be corrected |
| Height `H`, injected storage failure after any mutation | `OcompLifecycleBegin` | storage and ordered events equal pre-call state | exact retry from the same parent yields canonical success |
| Height `H`, all four effects already match exactly | exact retry | no-op success | idempotent only for exact state |
| Height `H`, partial or conflicting state | exact retry/activation | no mutation | fatal, fail-closed |
| Height `> H` | normal lifecycle | no reinstallation; normal expiry/request lifecycle only | restart/replay reads canonical installed state |
| Restart below/across/above `H` | canonical replay | node rejoins after replaying the same install | proof uses install identity and real OCOMP behavior, not Update version |
| Mismatched manifest at `H` | block import/execution | mismatched node cannot cross canonical activation | canonical committee progresses; mismatch remains isolated |
| Any height | independent real generic Update | normal Update semantics and registered future migrations apply | unrelated to OCOMP genesis activation |

### Canonical forms and compatibility

- `OcompForkInstallV1` is unchanged.
- Metadosis, ValidatorSet, Tribute, Oracle, and Update storage layouts are unchanged.
- No synthetic protocol-v1 Update proposal exists in fresh OCOMP genesis state.
- Generic active protocol version remains `ProtocolVersion::ZERO` after OCOMP activation.
- E2E-only `OcompForkRestartEvidenceV1` and `OcompForkMismatchEvidenceV1` drop fields that claim OCOMP activation through generic active-version values. Existing install hashes, activation/replay heights, fail-closed head separation, and an actual post-H OCOMP request provide the evidence. These harness artifacts are regenerated; they are not consensus wire.

### Ownership

- `outbe-metadosis::commands::install_fork_profile`: sole cross-module atomic activation command.
- ValidatorSet: founder registration validation/storage.
- Metadosis fork module: immutable request profile and protocol bundle authority.
- Tribute and Oracle modules: their own fresh-profile preconditions and idempotence.
- EVM begin-block route: exact activation-height ordering and mutation entitlement.
- EVM Update registry: generic Update integration, with no OCOMP handler.
- E2E harness: genesis fixture composition and restart/mismatch behavioral evidence.
- Existing OCOMP ADR/flow: normative documentation.

## Test-first implementation order

### 1. Freeze failing tests/evidence first

- Extend `commands.rs` tests to require all four owner effects after `install_fork_profile`.
- Expand mutation fault injection to prove rollback and exact retry across the complete mutation count, including Tribute and Oracle writes.
- Add partial/conflicting-state cases for each external profile.
- Change the EVM request-lifecycle fixture so it schedules no Update, expects active protocol version `0`, and proves block-H install plus an immediately reachable OCOMP request.
- Remove generic-version fields/assertions from restart and mismatch evidence; retain exact install identity, replay, progress/isolation, and actual OCOMP execution.

### 2. Production implementation

- In `crates/core/metadosis/src/commands.rs`, invoke ValidatorSet, Metadosis, Tribute, and Oracle initialization inside the existing `commit_transition::<MetadosisForkProfile>` checkpoint. Reuse the owner APIs; add no raw slot writes.
- In `crates/blockchain/evm/src/handlers.rs`, delete `OcompPocFreshDevnetHandler`, its version constant, and handler-specific tests. Keep `handlers::update::registry()` backed by `static ACTIVE_UPGRADE_HANDLERS: UpgradeHandlers = &[]`, so executor wiring and generic Update behavior stay intact.
- Keep `OcompLifecycleBegin`, its exact-height entitlement, `activation_height = 1`, and generic `UpdateLifecycle::begin_block_with_handlers` unchanged.

### 3. Harness and documentation

- Remove `schedule_protocol_v1_update`, proposal-id derivation, Update storage copying, imports, and scheduled-update fixture tests from `testing/e2e-harness/src/world/ocomp.rs`.
- Update restart/mismatch scenarios in `testing/e2e-harness/src/features/ocomp.rs` to stop querying `IUpdate.getActiveVersion` as OCOMP evidence.
- Rewrite the existing `docs/adr/system/ADR-S-OCM-004-certified-activation-job-fsm-and-protocol-versioning.md` section that assigns initialization to Update; do not add a new ADR.
- Update `docs/flows/002-off-chain-poc-protocol-flow.md` and stale owner comments in Metadosis/Tribute/Oracle.

## Approved file map and hot-file budget

Expected semantic production paths:

- `crates/core/metadosis/src/commands.rs` — pass 1 implementation/tests; pass 2 integration correction only.
- `crates/blockchain/evm/src/handlers.rs` — pass 1 removal/tests; pass 2 integration correction only.

Expected test/harness paths:

- `crates/blockchain/evm/tests/ocomp_request_lifecycle.rs`
- `testing/e2e-harness/src/world/ocomp.rs`
- `testing/e2e-harness/src/features/ocomp.rs`
- regenerated OCOMP evidence fixtures only if the scenarios serialize changed evidence.

Expected documentation/comment paths:

- `docs/adr/system/ADR-S-OCM-004-certified-activation-job-fsm-and-protocol-versioning.md`
- `docs/flows/002-off-chain-poc-protocol-flow.md`
- `crates/core/metadosis/src/schema.rs`
- `crates/core/tribute/src/state.rs` only if it contains stale fork-handler ownership text
- `crates/system/oracle/src/api.rs`

title: Route LocalNet lifecycle through the Rust E2E harness
description: Restore the documented debug LocalNet workflow through the canonical Rust harness. The persistent harness driver owns MongoDB, enclaves and validator processes; bootstrap uses seed_genesis.py plus current dynamic OCOMP founder registrations. prepare_network.py remains testnet/production-only.
design:
ARCHITECTURE FREEZE

Scope:
- Add a persistent operator interface on the canonical Rust E2E harness: outbe-e2e localnet bootstrap|start|serve|status|stop.
- Route mise localnet-bootstrap/start/status/stop through that interface.
- The documented debug workflow builds every required debug binary, bootstraps with seed_genesis.py, installs dynamic OCOMP founder registrations for the complete genesis ACTIVE ValidatorSet, binds GramineDirectDev TEE genesis, starts a managed MongoDB plus four mock enclaves/validators, proves every RPC advances, and stops only resources owned by this localnet.
- Keep the existing engine build fix and this LocalNet restoration in the current branch, per user direction.

Explicit non-goals:
- No changes to prepare_network.py or testnet/production deployment.
- No consensus, ValidatorSet, OCOMP voting, DCAP, worker/supervisor, wire-format, or chain-state semantic changes.
- No legacy fallback from the harness to run-testnet.sh/bootstrap-testnet.sh.
- No release build requirement and no SGX production evidence.

Invariants:
1. Local dev genesis is created only by dkg bootstrap + seed_genesis.py.
2. Every reachable TEE mode receives mandatory ocompForkInstallV1 before teeAttestationV1.
3. OCOMP founder registrations cover exactly the genesis ACTIVE ValidatorSet and use current validator address + consensus BLS MinPk inputs; they never define independent membership.
4. Bootstrap is fresh/idempotent only after an owned prior driver is stopped; it never kills unrelated processes.
5. One serve process owns MongoDB, every enclave, and every validator guard for the entire running lifetime.
6. All enclave endpoints are ready before any validator starts; validators are then spawned as one cohort.
7. start succeeds only after all configured RPCs are reachable and block production has advanced beyond genesis; an early child exit fails startup with log evidence.
8. status derives truth from the owned driver record plus live RPC observations; stale state is reported, never treated as running.
9. stop targets the exact recorded driver identity and waits for teardown; repeated stop is success.
10. Paths derive from repo/data-dir configuration. prepare_network.py and /srv-style deployment paths are never used.

Transition matrix:
- ABSENT + bootstrap -> BOOTSTRAPPED; writes keys/genesis/OCOMP/TEE manifest.
- ABSENT + start/status -> error/not-running; no implicit bootstrap.
- BOOTSTRAPPED + bootstrap -> replace only after proving no owned driver is live.
- BOOTSTRAPPED + start -> STARTING; spawn persistent serve process.
- STARTING + all enclaves ready -> launch validator cohort.
- STARTING + all RPCs advance -> RUNNING; publish atomic LocalnetStateV1.
- STARTING + child/config/readiness failure -> STOPPED; guards teardown, retain logs, nonzero result.
- RUNNING + start -> idempotent already-running success.
- RUNNING + status -> report driver/RPC heights.
- RUNNING + stop/SIGTERM -> stop nodes, enclaves, MongoDB; remove live state; STOPPED.
- stale PID/state + status -> STALE; no signal.
- stale PID/state + stop -> clean stale ownership record only after identity check.

Replay/restart/deadline:
- bootstrap rerun is deterministic in workflow shape but creates fresh keys/genesis.
- start after stop reuses bootstrapped datadirs.
- readiness is bounded; timeout tears down the partial start.
- driver crash leaves an identifiable stale record; status/stop fail closed against PID reuse using recorded process-start identity.

Canonical local state:
LocalnetStateV1 JSON under OUT_DIR contains version, owner pid, owner process-start identity, repo/data-dir, validator count, tee mode, fixed resolved RPC ports, phase, and latest observed heights. Written atomically; not chain state or wire protocol.

Ownership/file map and hot-file passes:
- testing/e2e-harness/src/localnet_driver.rs: sole operator lifecycle/state owner (new, one implementation pass + integration correction).
- testing/e2e-harness/src/main.rs: CLI dispatch only (one pass).

- mise.toml: task routing/debug mock build (one pass).
- README.md and existing LocalNet/runbook documentation: replace shell workflow with canonical harness commands (one pass).
- prepare_network.py, consensus and production crates are outside the approved map.

Tests/evidence, test-first by vertical slice:
- CLI/state unit tests: canonical commands, atomic state, stale/live owner identity, idempotent stop.
- Bootstrap characterization: mock/GramineDirect also invokes current OCOMP genesis before TEE binding; no static OCOMP fields.
- Start ordering test through an injected launch recorder: every enclave-ready event precedes the first validator spawn.
- Command integration: debug build; localnet-bootstrap; localnet-start; all four RPC heights >0 and increasing; status; stop; no owned processes remain.

PR boundary:
One functionally complete PR on the current fix/ocomp-http-engine-build branch, explicitly requested by the user: engine compiles and the documented LocalNet workflow actually boots and runs. Coherent commits may separate engine and LocalNet. No production route switches until the persistent driver path is complete and tested.

title: Work 3: make Metadosis day failures recoverable
description: Audit and plan a deterministic recovery path for Metadosis errors that currently surface as fatal precompile failures and can halt CycleTick/network progress. A failed Metadosis worldwide day must become Failed without reverting the enclosing transaction or stopping the node, and its unspent retained lysis budget must be credited once to PromiseLimit. Include the OFFCHAIN_PENDING window-expiry mismatch at runtime.rs as the motivating reproduced case.
design: Revised requirement: crates/core/metadosis must contain no PrecompileError::Fatal constructors or local fatal/reject helpers. errors.rs is the sole Metadosis error vocabulary and owns stable day-failure, ingress-rejection and module-failure codes plus boundary mappings. Internal code returns MetadosisResult. Once a production command has resolved an exact WWD, any Metadosis semantic/invariant error rolls back that day's attempted effects, atomically marks the WWD FAILED, credits the exact unspent amount to PromiseLimit, cleans its OCOMP state and returns success to the enclosing critical system transaction. Invalid public calldata remains a centralized RevertBytes rejection. Provider/storage/body-read failures are not Metadosis semantic errors and cannot be converted into consensus WWD failure; they propagate in their native non-Fatal variants. Commands with no WWD context such as profile installation must contain module failure without inventing a WWD.
acceptance_criteria: An evidence-based implementation plan identifies the exact recoverable error boundary, atomic failed-day transition, one-time carry-over accounting, transaction/non-revert semantics, invariants, call sites and tests. No implementation is performed before user approval.
notes: User clarified that eliminating network-level Fatal behavior is a module contract, not merely a fix for exact-height cases. Current inventory has local Fatal construction/helpers throughout aggregate, commit, lifecycle, settlement, terminal, genesis and ocomp files; OCOMP also duplicates reject codes/helpers. submitLysisResult has void success ABI, so after valid vote/job identification an internal WWD failure can terminalize the day and return empty success, while malformed or unauthorized caller input remains RevertBytes. Implementation should end with an rg gate proving no PrecompileError::Fatal, fn fatal or local reject helper remains under crates/core/metadosis/src outside tests, with all stable error definitions in errors.rs.

description: On the exact frozen testnet release, generate a new one-use non-zero binding, capture one intent-bound Processor-CA SGX quote and post-run collateral, and verify it through the public enclave-resident verifier at the release consensus timestamp. A real Platform-CA node presents its own evidence only when it joins.

For each accepted capture choose a fresh random nonzero one-use binding ID, construct the exact canonical Validator or FullNode registration intent, generate the quote inside the NodeHost-authorized gramine-sgx enclave, then acquire all eight collateral components after the run begins. Verify through the public enclave-resident V1 verifier at a recorded consensus timestamp. Produce one accepted Processor-CA result and one accepted registered multi-package Platform-CA result. Record CPU model, SGX/EPC, quote identity, MRENCLAVE, MRSIGNER, ISV product and SVN, policy hash, QVL and Gramine versions, collateral issue and expiry, CRL issuer and type, byte size, SHA-256, verdict and artifact paths. title: Queued tx lifetime eviction violates no-silent-drops contract
description:
ID: E2E-TXPOOL-EVICT-LOG-001
Status: confirmed-product-defect
Observed: A public-RPC transaction with nonce gap 64 is accepted into the queued pool, remains present while an ordinary transfer mines, then is evicted by the configured queued-lifetime bound on every validator. No node emits a reason-bearing eviction record; the E2E fails only the final logging postcondition.
Expected: ADR-B-TXP-001 amendment decision 4 and crates/blockchain/txpool/README require every eviction to log tx hash, sender, nonce and reason; no silent drops.
Production reachability: Ordinary public eth_sendRawTransaction, upstream Reth queued subpool and the Outbe default 120-second queued lifetime/no-locals policy.
Reproduction command: release outbe-e2e, tee=sgx-no-attest, sudo=true, scenario 'A transaction that can never be mined is evicted from every pool'.
SHA/environment: main fixed point dce3a1ae8a8f412ed05b6449fe3db753c0e3b261; real four-validator SGX/no-attest chain_id 54322345.
Evidence: /tmp/e2e-remaining-harness/run-1787573520-635655/scenario-1. All functional steps through eviction on every validator pass; the exact final failure is 'validator-0 evicted the transaction without logging a reason'. The initial aggregate scenario 29 reproduced the same result.
Test setup validity: The transaction is produced through the public signed RPC path, is observed in the pool, and the test proves the chain remains live with a concurrently mined ordinary transfer.
Affected invariant/postcondition: Every node-local pool eviction is observable with exact transaction identity and reason.
Competing causes excluded: Failure is not eviction timing or propagation because absence from every pool is asserted after the lifetime; not chain stall because ordinary transfer mined and committee stayed live; not missing custom pending-staleness logging because this transaction is queued and removed by the upstream lifetime path.
Root cause: Outbe's structured logging exists only in maintain_outbe_pool for two-snapshot pending eviction. The separately configured upstream queued-lifetime path removes transactions without an Outbe reason-bearing log seam.
Counterfactual proof: Routing queued-lifetime removal through an owned callback/maintenance seam that emits the frozen structured record would preserve the already-passing eviction behavior and satisfy the only failing assertion.
Proposed minimal fix: Architecture-controlled txpool observability change; no product edit is authorized in this E2E goal. Do not weaken the E2E or whitelist silence.
Regression: Keep the exact public-RPC unreachable-nonce scenario and assert one structured lifetime reason per node that actually held/evicted it; preserve pending stale/descendant reasons.
Verdict scope: Confirmed for queued-subpool lifetime eviction; pending two-snapshot logging already exists and is not implicated.
acceptance_criteria: Queued-lifetime eviction emits a structured tx_hash/sender/nonce/reason record without changing pool or consensus semantics; focused unit/provider tests and the release E2E pass while pending-staleness reasons remain intact.
close_reason: Faithful RED reproduced; frozen minimal fix implemented; focused/package/clippy gates and release SGX/no-attest E2E with clean shutdown log audit passed.
